items.title: WARRI DELINEATION: Lawyer seeks probe, warns against political manipulation, violence
items.description: Lawyer and politician, Chief Robinson Ariyo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to investigate the Warri delineation exercise, saying there are allegations of financial inducement to favour some areas over others. Ariyo also called on the President to direct the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice to provide an independent written legal opinion on the legality of the exercise. In a statement, he urged the President to direct relevant agencies to preserve all documents and records relating to the exercise and investigate allegations of financial misconduct, security compromises and electoral irregularities. He further called for an independent forensic audit of private surveillance contracts relating to Nigeria’s oil and gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta, particularly those whose financial transactions, beneficiaries or performance records might be connected to the allegations surrounding the Warri delineation controversy. Ariyo also urged the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, ICPC, and Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit, NFIU, to investigate credible allegations of suspicious dollar transactions, unexplained financial inflows and possible financial inducement of political actors, public officers, electoral personnel and security operatives in connection with the controversy. The statement reads: “That the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice be requested to provide an independent, written legal opinion on the legality of the ongoing Warri delineation exercise, identifying the applicable constitutional provisions, statutory powers, judicial orders and procedural requirements governing the exercise. The opinion should specifically distinguish between the delineation of electoral wards, State Constituencies and Federal Constituencies. “That INEC be formally requested, in the exercise of its constitutional independence, to publish the complete delineation report, supporting maps, methodology, relevant population and geographical data, stakeholder submissions and reasons for accepting or rejecting material objections. That the Commission be urged to undertake a transparent review of any substantiated procedural or factual irregularities and refrain from implementing any aspect found to be unlawful, subject always to applicable judicial orders and statutory requirements. “That all relevant documents, correspondence, meeting records, maps, electronic records, financial documents and administrative communications relating to the exercise be preserved against destruction, alteration or concealment. “That the appropriate federal authorities undertake an independent forensic audit of private surveillance contracts relating to Nigeria’s oil and gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta, particularly contracts whose financial transactions, beneficiaries or performance records may be relevant to the allegations raised herein. The audit should cover contract awards, disbursements, beneficial ownership, subcontracting arrangements, foreign-currency transactions and evidence of possible diversion of public funds, an independent scrutiny and examination of the oil production and sales by the NNPC within the period in view to determine whether or not there are leakages and if there are, the extent of such leakages. “That the EFCC, ICPC, and NFIU, within their respective statutory mandates, investigate credible allegations of suspicious dollar transactions, unexplained financial inflows, and possible financial inducement of political actors, public officers, electoral personnel, or security operatives in connection with the Warri delineation controversy. “That the National Security Adviser, in collaboration with the relevant security agencies, conduct an impartial assessment of possible security compromises, threats to lives and property, and any evidence of inducement or improper influence involving security operatives in the affected areas. “That adequate and impartial security measures be maintained in Warri North, Warri South and Warri South-West Local Government Areas to protect all residents, traditional institutions and legitimate community interests, irrespective of ethnic affiliation. “That Your Excellency convene a genuinely inclusive stakeholder engagement involving recognised traditional rulers, community representatives, relevant political stakeholders, legal practitioners and other affected interests from the Itsekiri, Ijaw and Urhobo communities. Such engagement must not be used to impose a predetermined outcome but should provide an opportunity for all parties to present their grievances and supporting evidence. “That persons who provide credible information concerning financial misconduct, security compromise or electoral irregularities be afforded appropriate protection against intimidation, harassment, victimisation or retaliation. “That the appropriate agencies be directed to provide an initial report of their findings and recommendations within a reasonable and publicly communicated timeframe, subject to the requirements of confidentiality and due process. “Your Excellency, history will not merely remember the number of infrastructure projects executed or the economic policies implemented during an administration. It will also remember how that administration protected the Constitution, defended democratic institutions, and responded to credible allegations of abuse of public power. “The Niger Delta has contributed immeasurably to our country’s economic survival. Its people deserve fairness, justice, security and equitable political representation. The Warri delineation controversy must not become another chapter in the history of avoidable communal antagonism, political manipulation and institutional distrust. It would be deeply unfortunate if an exercise intended to improve electoral representation were to become a source of division, suspicion and possible violence. I respectfully remind Your Excellency that the Constitution is supreme and binding on all authorities and persons under Section 1(1) and (3) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended). “To demonstrate how unambiguous the governing provisions of the Constitution on the subject matter are, I humbly reproduce it as follows: Section 115: Time when alteration of State Constituencies takes effect. Where the boundaries of any State constituency established under section 112 of this Constitution are altered in accordance with the provisions of section 114 of this Constitution, that alteration shall come into effect after it has been approved by the National Assembly and after the current life of the House of Assembly”. “The issue is whether, having regard to the combined provisions of Sections 112, 113, 114 and 115 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) possesses the power to bring into effect an alteration of the boundaries of an existing State Constituency without the requisite approval of the National Assembly and before the expiration of the current life of the relevant State House of Assembly.” The post WARRI DELINEATION: Lawyer seeks probe, warns against political manipulation, violence appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NIMC arrests illegal NIN operators, seizes enrolment equipment
items.description: By Emmanuel Elebeke The National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) has intensified its crackdown on illegal National Identification Number (NIN) enrolment, unauthorised data modification and extortion, following an enforcement operation that led to several arrests in Gwagwalada and other locations. The Commission disclosed this in a statement, saying its Inspectorate Compliance and Enforcement Unit (ICEU) carried out the operation and seized equipment allegedly used for illegal enrolment activities. It said the exercise was part of efforts to curb unauthorised enrolment and unethical practices while protecting the integrity, security and credibility of Nigeria’s National Identity Management System. NIMC noted that many of the challenges encountered by NIN holders resulted from attempts to bypass official enrolment procedures. It stressed that NIN enrolment could only be conducted at its approved centres, while requests for modification of personal data could be processed through its self-service modification platform. The Commission also advised NIN holders to download the NINAuth application from the iOS App Store or Google Play Store to access security features, print their NIN slips and enjoy other related services. The Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of NIMC, Engr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote, reiterated the Commission’s zero tolerance for extortion and unethical practices. She said the Commission remained committed to providing seamless and hitch-free NIN enrolment services for Nigerians and legal residents. NIMC urged applicants and existing NIN holders to use only its approved channels for enrolment and other related services. It advised members of the public to visit www.nimc.gov.ng or follow its verified social media platforms for accurate information. The post NIMC arrests illegal NIN operators, seizes enrolment equipment appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: AI not enemy of democracy — Amupitan
items.description: THE Chairman of Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, has defended the use of Artificial Intelligence in election management. According to him, the technology is not a threat to democracy, despite its potential misuse by malicious actors. Amupitan said AI could improve electoral administration through efficient voter registration, logistics planning, data analysis and the management of large voter databases. He warned that advances in generative AI had made it easier to create deceptive content capable of undermining public confidence in elections. The INEC chairman, who stated these at The Beyond the Ballot Summit in Abuja yesterday, explained that electoral management bodies worldwide had adopted AI-assisted processes to improve administrative efficiency and strengthen election planning. The INEC chairman’s remarks came amid preparations for the 2027 general election, with the commission recently announcing plans to integrate AI into Nigeria’s electoral system. He said: “Artificial Intelligence, AI, is not an enemy of democracy.” He, however, expressed concern over the growing accessibility of generative AI tools which, he said, could be exploited to manipulate voters and spread disinformation during elections. “However, the rabid democratisation of generative AI models has dramatically lowered the barrier to entry for malicious actors, capacities, capabilities that want to require speedy-level intelligence resources such as high voice cloning of public figures, hyper realistic synthesis of election officials making false announcements are now accessible at negligible cost. These tools target specific vulnerabilities with distinct timelines,” Amupitan said. The growing use of AI in electoral processes has heightened concerns about the spread of fabricated announcements, manipulated audio recordings and realistic videos that could mislead voters, impersonate public officials and disrupt election administration. While the technology offers opportunities to improve the efficiency of election management, its potential misuse presents challenges for electoral integrity, particularly in an environment where false information can spread rapidly through social media. INEC’s planned adoption of AI, therefore, places renewed emphasis on the need to balance technological innovation with safeguards against misinformation, impersonation and other forms of digital manipulation. The commission noted that it would ensure that the technology strengthened the credibility, transparency and efficiency of the electoral process as Nigeria approached the 2027 polls. The controversy over the use of AI in elections intensified recently after suspicious photographs, including images believed to have been AI-generated, were found in INEC’s preliminary Register of Voters. The photographs, which appeared in some voter records in Etsako West Local Government Area of Edo State, raised questions about the integrity of the voter database and the processes used to capture and verify registration information. INEC subsequently acknowledged the questionable records and said it was investigating the circumstances surrounding the photographs. The commission’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, said some of the AI-generated images were linked to irregularities allegedly introduced by some registration officers who had access to the system. The post AI not enemy of democracy — Amupitan appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigeria needs leaders equipped for changing realities — Sam Adeyemi
items.description: By Ogochukwu Agha LAGOS—THE Senior Pastor of Daystar Christian Centre, Pastor Sam Adeyemi, yesterday, warned that Nigeria cannot afford leaders who learn on the job, lamenting that many occupying positions of authority have never received formal leadership training, despite the country’s mounting economic and social challenges. Adeyemi spoke in Lagos ahead of the 2026 edition of the church’s annual Excellence in Leadership Conference (ELC), scheduled for November 5 and 6, 2026, at the Daystar Christian Centre, Oregun in Lagos. Making a case for deliberate leadership development, he said: “Sometimes only God knows who is going to be governor. Who knows who is going to be senator tomorrow? And most people occupying leadership positions in our country have not learned leadership anywhere.” He urged Nigerians to take advantage of the conference, themed ‘Leading in Uncertainty’, describing participation as “a great investment in their lives. In a joint message, Adeyemi and his wife, Nike Adeyemi, who co-host the conference, said the event would explore “what it truly means to lead when the ground keeps shifting economically, socially, and personally. “Previous participants have described the conference as a game-changer, with some attributing practical improvements in their careers and businesses to lessons acquired at the event”, the statement reads. They explained that the theme was informed by prevailing realities, including volatile markets, rising living costs, policy changes and transformations in the world of work, against the backdrop of an approaching general election cycle. “Participants would be equipped to stand firm, think clearly, and lead boldly, while learning how to turn uncertainty into a leadership advantage,” they added. The post Nigeria needs leaders equipped for changing realities — Sam Adeyemi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: One dead, four arrested as illegal miners clash with NAIMOS operatives in Atiwa Forest Reserve
items.description: One suspected illegal miner has been killed and another injured after a group of suspected illegal miners opened fire on operatives of Operation GREEN SHIELD during an enforcement operation in the Atiwa Forest Reserve. Four suspects — three Malian nationals and a Ghanaian — were arrested following the armed confrontation. An operational account said the incident occurred on Monday, November 2, when operatives from the Army Special Operations Brigade (ASOB) team advanced about 10 kilometres into the forest to another suspected illegal mining site identified through drone surveillance. The foot patrol, which lasted from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., led the team to a site where about 50 suspected illegal miners were reportedly working. On seeing the operatives, some of the miners attempted to flee, while others allegedly opened fire on the patrol team. The operatives returned fire, killing one of the suspected miners and injuring another. Two pump-action guns and six rounds of ammunition were also seized during the encounter. The injured suspect was given first aid by the operatives before being evacuated to the Kyebi Government Hospital for further medical attention. The four arrested suspects were subsequently handed over to the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) for further action. No casualties were recorded among the enforcement team.

items.title: 'Who cares?' Alaska voters shrug off potential Democratic manipulation
items.description: In the long line of US midterm voters casting ballots early Monday in Anchorage, Alaska’s largest city, everyone was aware of the whiff of scandal surrounding the election. Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola, in a tight race against Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan that could determine who controls Congress in Washington, stands accused of recruiting another Dan Sullivan to run in order to create ballot confusion and siphon off votes from the senator. Very few people braving near-freezing conditions in Anchorage appeared concerned about the revelations first reported by The New York Times , which landed like a thunderclap in political circles thousands of miles away. But in the far northwestern state of Alaska, voter Dale Brown summed up the feeling succinctly: “Who cares?” The 25-year-old carpenter considered the decoy ploy “immoral,” but said he knows “it’s not illegal technically” and that Republicans have used the same tactics, recruiting ghost candidates in Florida’s 2020 Senate race. US Sen. Dan Sullivan speaks to supporters during a campaign rally on November 02, 2026 in Wasilla, Alaska. —Getty Images via AFP “American politics has gone to this absolute dog-and-pony show of lies,” independent voter Brown told AFP , adding: “I think that any kind of moral (conscience) is long gone.” The controversy “won’t change anything” about his choice though — Brown cast his ballot for Democrats, saying he’s fed up with inflation under President Donald Trump. Trump has cried foul in Alaska, as the crucial race could cost his party its Senate majority. It is a bitter battle in Anchorage, where rival campaign signs are seen on either side of neighbours’ fences. ‘Pretty clear’ Following the Times account that Peltola’s campaign helped orchestrate the scheme — although the candidate denied any knowledge of it — the president has sought to preemptively challenge the election results. A federal judge rejected that bid on Sunday, but the pressure from the Trump administration has continued. Federal authorities have since launched a criminal investigation, although they have refused to explain its legal basis. At a shopping centre overlooking snow-capped mountains, Rae Hart approached the polling station acknowledging that it could be “confusing potentially” to have a ballot featuring two Dan Sullivans. But few appeared fooled by the deception, the Republican voter said. “I heard people in line saying, ‘Be sure to vote for the right Dan Sullivan,’” said Hart, a 37-year-old criminal investigator. Campaign signs are displayed outside a campaign event for US Sen. Dan Sullivan on November 2, 2026 in Wasilla, Alaska. —Getty Images via AFP Many voters interviewed by AFP in Alaska said they have been inundated for weeks with flyers, ads and other mail regarding the controversial election. On the ballot, the Sullivans are clearly distinguishable. The senator’s name is accompanied by the labels “registered Republican” and “incumbent,” while Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr. — the “fake” Sullivan, as Trump calls him — shows no political affiliation. Poll workers prepared in advance to answer questions clarifying the situation. But a volunteer at the polling place confided, on condition of anonymity, that “it seems like people are pretty clear”. ‘Distractive tactics’ Airline pilot Luke Clement agreed, saying: “It’s pretty clear on the ballot who is who.” The 47-year-old, however, did regret that this year’s campaign has slid into ugly “mudslinging” instead of focusing on the issues. Clement was particularly concerned about persistent inflation, fueled by Trump’s war on Iran . Alaskans feel it more acutely than other Americans, he said, because the state’s distance means “everything is shipped in, and everything is dependent on fuel costs”. Others in line could be heard discussing the decline of salmon populations driven by overfishing and climate change, and the extent to which the state’s vast oil riches should be exploited. Ultimately, the scandal surrounding Peltola is being used as “distractive tactics” to divert voters away from what’s at stake, said surgical technologist Zara Oakley, 41. Alaska is seen as a conservative stronghold, but dissatisfaction with Trump is so widespread here that the Senate Democratic challenger is neck-and-neck with the incumbent senator in the polls. Oakley said she is not surprised Trump is seeking to cast doubt on election results, as he has done in several other US states. “He seeks to destroy democracy,” she said. “I don’t think it has anything to do with what is principled or what’s right or what’s just. “

items.title: Maaz Sadaqat, Hasan Nawaz named in Pakistan Shaheens squad for Rising Stars Asia Cup
items.description: Maaz Sadaqat and Hasan Nawaz have been included in the 15-member Pakistan Shaheens squad for the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, with Abdul Samad appointed captain for the 50-over tournament to be held in Qatar from Nov 19 to 29. The Pakistan Cricket Board announced the squad on Tuesday, with the Shaheens set to defend the title they won in the previous 50-over edition in 2023. Pakistan are also the defending champions of the T20 version of the competition, having beaten Bangladesh A in a final decided by a Super Over. The eight-team tournament will feature two groups of four sides. Pakistan have been placed in Group ‘B’ alongside India A, Nepal and the United Arab Emirates, while Group ‘A’ comprises Afghanistan A, Bangladesh A, Hong Kong China and Sri Lanka A. The Shaheens will open their campaign against the UAE on Nov 20, before taking on India A two days later and Nepal on Nov 24. Their first match will be played at the University of Doha Science and Technology ground, with the remaining group fixtures scheduled at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium. All three group matches are day-night fixtures except the opening game, which will be played during the day. The semi-finals are scheduled for Nov 26 and 27, with the final to be held on Nov 29. Samad will lead a batting group that includes Maaz, Hasan, Haider Ali, Shahzaib Khan, Farhan Yousuf and Shamyl Hussain. Rohail Nazir has been named as the designated wicket-keeper. The squad also includes three spin options in left-arm spin all-rounder Danish Aziz, leg-spinner Saad Masood and Sufyan Moqim. The pace attack will be led by Mohammad Hasnain and also features Ahmed Daniyal, Akif Javed and Muhammad Imran Randhawa. Ahmed Daniyal was part of the Shaheens side that won the previous T20 edition, playing a key role as the team clinched the title against Bangladesh A in a Super Over. Pakistan won the last 50-over edition in Sri Lanka in 2023, beating India A by 128 runs in the final. They were runners-up in the opening two editions in 2013 and 2017 before winning the competition in 2019. The Shaheens will be aiming to retain their title against a field that includes several of the region’s emerging sides, with a meeting against India A among the key fixtures in the group stage.

items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS—THE Lagos State government has warned residents against dumping waste into canals and drainage channels, cautioning that the illegal practice severely threatens public sanitation and heightens the risk of flash flooding across the state. The Head of Service, Bode Agoro, gave the warning during the October edition of the state’s monthly environmental sanitation exercise. He urged council chairman and community leaders to actively mobilize residents to improve environmental standards in their domains. He stressed that “maintaining environmental hygiene requires continuous civic commitment.” Agoro stated that officials personally observed residents discarding refuse into local waterways during the exercise. While the Ministry of the Environment has been alerted to clear the clogged channels and plans are being drawn up with drainage authorities to reconstruct key infrastructure in affected areas, Agoro warned that engineering solutions “will fail if indiscriminate waste disposal continues.” The post Drainage: Lagos govt warns against indiscriminate refuse dumping appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tinubu to unveil book on Olanipekun’s landmark cases
items.description: By Henry Ojelu LAGOS—PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu will on November 19 unveil a six-volume publication documenting landmark cases handled by renowned legal practitioner, Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN, over his 50 years in the Nigerian legal profession. The publication, titled ‘Wole Olanipekun through the cases’, examines Olanipekun’s contributions to the development of Nigerian law and jurisprudence through commentaries on significant cases he handled during his five decades at the Bar. The unveiling will take place at the WOC Justice Summit, an initiative of Wole Olanipekun & Co, which brings together stakeholders to deliberate on issues affecting the justice sector. The event will take place 24 hours after Olanipekun’s 75th birthday, having been born on November 18, 1951. The six-volume publication features forewords by the Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, and the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN. It brings together contributions from retired judicial officers, academics, Senior Advocates of Nigeria and other prominent legal practitioners, offering an examination of the breadth of Olanipekun’s legal practice. and his influence on the country’s jurisprudence. The legal luminary is currently Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council of the University of Lagos, having previously held similar positions at the University of Ibadan and Ajayi Crowther University. He is also Chairman of the Board of Trustees of Ajayi Crowther University and Chancellor of Bamidele Olumilua University of Education, Science and Technology, Ikere-Ekiti. The post Tinubu to unveil book on Olanipekun’s landmark cases appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Osborne Foreshore drama: Lagos dep gov locked out by developer
items.description: *Residents accuse developer of canal encroachment, harassment By Godwin Oritse LAGOS—IN a dramatic development that has raised concerns over compliance with planning regulations in Lagos State, the Deputy Governor, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, was reportedly locked out of a disputed construction site at Osborne Foreshore Phase II Estate, Ikoyi, on Saturday by Kenshad International Ltd, a developer facing allegations of planning violations and environmental infractions from residents. Hamzat, accompanied by a high-powered delegation of government officials and political leaders, waited for more than 30 minutes at the entrance of the development named Abba Court on Mahogany Close, but the gates were shut. The incident occurred during a visit prompted by complaints from residents, who accused the developer of engaging in unauthorised activities they said could threaten the safety and environmental integrity of the estate. “Why did he refuse to allow the Deputy Governor and his team in if he has nothing to hide?” a resident asked, expressing suspicion over the incident. The Deputy Governor expressed displeasure over the developer’s conduct and assured residents that the Lagos State Government would investigate the complaints. At a meeting with Hamzat tagged ‘Osborne Phase II residents and public leaders’ dialogue,’ residents accused the developer of constructing beneath high-tension electricity lines, constructing slabs over a canal, and carrying out sand-filling activities that have narrowed the water outlets in the estate. Speaking on behalf of the residents, Mr. Adebisi Taiwo alleged that the developer created an unauthorised back gate through which thugs were brought into the estate to intimidate those who questioned its activities. Taiwo also accused the developer of using security agents and unscrupulous officials to harass and intimidate them. The residents urged on the state government to investigate the allegations against Kenshad International and its owner and take appropriate action. “The developer had relied on a purported joint-venture arrangement with the Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development to justify its activities. “The Lagos State Government must re-examine the arrangement and establish whether the project has complied with the applicable rules.” Responding to the complaints, Hamzat stressed that land use, physical planning and development control fall within the jurisdiction of state governments. Citing Supreme Court rulings, he argued that the Federal Government cannot simply assume the role of a state town-planning authority or issue building permits in place of the relevant state authorities. He pledged that the state government would look into the developer’s activities. Hamzat was accompanied on the visit by former Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Wale Edun; Senator Wasiu Eshilokun Sanni, representing Lagos Central Senatorial District; Hon. Gbolahan Yishawu, representing Eti-Osa Constituency in the Lagos State House of Assembly; commissioners and others. The post Osborne Foreshore drama: Lagos dep gov locked out by developer appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: PAMA backs FG’s commitment to affordable long-term industrial financing
items.description: By Yinka Kolawole The Pan African Manufacturers Association (PAMA) has welcomed the Federal Government’s commitments to improve energy supply, provide affordable long-term financing for industries, strengthen local procurement, secure industrial corridors and establish quarterly engagements with manufacturers. According to the association, these priorities align with its broader commitment to advancing industrialisation, strengthening regional value chains and expanding intra-African trade. However, it stressed that effective implementation of the commitments would be critical to improving the operating environment for manufacturers, boosting industrial productivity and strengthening Nigeria’s competitiveness in regional and global markets. PAMA stated this while commending the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) for the successful hosting of its 54th Annual General Meeting (AGM). Held under the theme, “Leveraging National Industrial Policy to Position Nigeria as Africa’s Industrial Hub,” the AGM focused on implementing the Nigeria Industrial Policy 2025 (NIP 2025), enhancing manufacturing competitiveness, expanding access to industrial finance, reducing energy costs and promoting local value addition. A major highlight of the event was the 6th Adeola Odutola Lecture, delivered by Dr. Kandeh Kolleh Yumkella, former Director-General of the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO). Discussions at the meeting emphasised the need to translate industrial policy commitments into tangible economic outcomes through effective implementation, institutional accountability and sustained collaboration between the public and private sectors. PAMA reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening partnership with MAN, noting that closer collaboration among manufacturers across Africa is essential to developing regional value chains, and expanding industrial capacity. and unlocking opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). It further emphasised the importance of building a competitive and integrated African manufacturing sector capable of driving sustainable economic growth, creating jobs and increasing the continent’s participation in regional and global trade. The post PAMA backs FG’s commitment to affordable long-term industrial financing appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Procurement knowledge gap shuts small businesses out of FG contracts — Minister
items.description: By Yinka Kolawole Many small businesses in Nigeria are missing out on Federal Government contracts due to inadequate knowledge of public procurement procedures, Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Enoh, has said. Enoh stated this in Abuja at the launch of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Public Procurement Training Programme and digital learning portal organised by the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), adding that limited knowledge, weak internal processes and inadequate capacity were hindering small businesses from competing effectively for government contracts. He said many entrepreneurs lacked the skills to register, meet compliance requirements, interpret procurement documents, prepare competitive bids and execute government contracts. “Many businesses are excluded because of capacity constraints, limited knowledge, weak internal processes and insufficient capability,” the minister said. Enoh added that some businesses were disqualified because of missing documents, while the complexity of procurement procedures further restricted their participation. He said the knowledge gap increased the cost of doing business and deepened small businesses’ dependence on intermediaries, stressing the need to give women-owned enterprises and other small businesses equal opportunities to compete. The minister urged business associations to publicise procurement opportunities and educate their members on bidding requirements. He also called on ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs) to simplify procurement procedures, improve transparency and strengthen support for small businesses. Director-General of BPP, Adebowale Adedokun, said MSMEs account for about 96 per cent of businesses in Nigeria and contribute approximately 50 per cent of the nation’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP). He said despite their economic importance, many face barriers to public procurement, including inadequate technical knowledge and difficulties navigating bidding requirements, adding that the digital learning portal would provide free training tailored to Nigeria’s procurement system. items.title: Pologne | Les dessous de la tentative de coup d’État de l’Européiste Tusk
items.description: La Pologne vient de connaître, vendredi 30 octobre 2026, ce que les médias et les analystes politiques ont qualifié de tentative de coup d‘État orchestrée par le Premier ministre Donald Tusk. Bien que l’opération ait échoué, elle dit beaucoup sur la mainmise que les technocrates de l’Union européenne (UE) veulent avoir sur les pays membres. Le libéral Tusk a été leur pion. Francesca de Villasmundo * Călin Georgescu, le vainqueur des élections en Roumanie, qui lui ont été volées par la suite, l’avait prédit : «Un coup porté en plein cœur de la démocratie, partout dans le monde ! Si la démocratie s’effondre en Roumanie, c’est l’ensemble du monde démocratique qui s’effondrera. Ce n’est que le début !» Il y a un an, Georgescu affirmait que toutes les capitales européennes seraient confrontées à au moins un coup d’État, faute d’avoir réagi à l’annulation de l’élection présidentielle en Roumanie. Ce qui se déroule depuis samedi dernier en Pologne correspond précisément à ce scénario : un coup d’État orchestré par le Premier ministre Tusk, la marionnette des technocrates de l’UE qui visent à bâtir une Europe fédérale au-dessus de la souveraineté des nations. Dans leur plan, le président conservateur polonais, Karol Nawrocki, élu en 2025, et proche du parti conservateur-nationaliste Droit et Justice (PiS), désireux de transformer l’UE en une union d’États-nations, est un grain de sable qu’il faut éliminer d’une manière ou d’une autre. Et tant pis pour l’État de droit que ces mêmes technocrates, Ursula von der Leyen en tête, brandissent quand cela leur permet de mettre des bâtons dans les roues des gouvernements souverainistes conservateurs. Le Tribunal constitutionnel polonais en point de mire Retour sur ce coup d’État qui a échoué : le gouvernement polonais néolibéral-centriste, dirigé Tusk, a tenté un coup d’État contre le Tribunal constitutionnel. Vendredi soir, la police a encerclé le bâtiment, a perquisitionné les locaux et a notifié une suspension d’un mois, émise par une juge, Korwin-Piotrowska, proche de Tusk, au président Bogdan Świeczkowski et à son adjoint qui furent empêché d’accéder à leurs bureaux. En parallèle, Mme Korwin-Piotrowska assuma leurs fonctions et fit déployer la police au palais de justice, tandis que le ministre de la Justice de Tusk demandait la levée de leur immunité et l’ouverture d’une procédure judiciaire à leur encontre. Des manifestants se rassemblèrent rapidement devant le bâtiment pour faire opposition à une opération qui n’a pas été du goût d’un grand nombre de Polonais, même parmi les partisans de Tusk. Un différend oppose en effet depuis plus de dix ans libéraux et conservateurs au sujet du Tribunal constitutionnel, que les libéraux et leurs alliés européens accusent les conservateurs de manipuler. En réalité, ce tribunal tend à privilégier le droit polonais au détriment du droit de l’UE. Le Tribunal constitutionnel polonais est chargé de vérifier la conformité des lois à la Constitution. Ses juges sont élus par le Parlement, mais leur nomination doit être confirmée par le président de la République. Le président Nawrocki a rejeté cinq des huit juges proposés par le gouvernement Tusk. Dans ce contexte, les prochaines élections législatives de l’automne 2027 pourraient voir les conservateurs revenir au pouvoir grâce à une coalition entre eux, leur nouvelle faction dissidente et les deux partis libertariens-nationalistes. Dans ce cas, soutenu par le Tribunal, proche des conservateurs, Nawrocki serait en mesure de remettre sur la table son programme de réforme de l’UE. Tentative européiste de mettre la main sur le Tribunal constitutionnel La dernière tentative de coup d’État a été orchestrée par Bruxelles et le gouvernement Tusk dans le but d’inverser ce processus en plaçant des juges européistes, avec Mme Korwin-Piotrowska à leur tête, au Tribunal Constitutionnel. La Pologne en passe de devenir l’un des pays les plus riches au monde Après l’annonce du coup d’État, le président Nawrocki est rentré à Varsovie, dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi, après avoir ordonné à son avion, à destination du Sénégal, d’opérer un demi-tour, comme il l’a annoncé sur le réseau social X. De retour en Pologne, le président polonais a ensuite rejoint le premier président du Tribunal, parvenant à franchir les cordons de police et à entrer dans le bâtiment de la Cour constitutionnelle samedi soir. Une fois à l’intérieur, il a destitué les cinq juges illégalement assermentés par Tusk et a autorisé le président de la Cour suprême à accéder à son bureau. Le président a ensuite publié une déclaration sur X condamnant la «violation de l’ordre constitutionnel» et «la prise de contrôle par la force d’un organe constitutionnel de l’État» . Déterminé à ne pas laisser l’UE gouverner la Pologne, il a exposé les raisons du coup d’État de Tusk téléguidé par l’UE : «L’objectif ultime est d’imposer le droit de l’UE sur le droit polonais, de forcer l’adoption du Pacte migratoire de l’UE et d’ouvrir les frontières de la Pologne à des dizaines de milliers, potentiellement des centaines de milliers, de migrants illégaux. […] Ils veulent détruire la position de la Pologne en tant que l’une des nations les plus sûres, les plus stables et les plus prospères d’Europe, exposant notre peuple aux difficultés économiques, à l’instabilité sociale et au chaos déjà vécus ailleurs en Europe. […] Pendant longtemps, le gouvernement a poussé la Pologne vers une confrontation dangereuse avec la Russie, et je rejette fermement cette direction. Après avoir échoué à convaincre le peuple polonais avec son programme, il recourt maintenant à des mesures désespérées, tentant de s’emparer d’une autre institution publique par des moyens illégaux.» Source : Media-Presse-info . * Journaliste et autrice collaborant principalement avec le site d’information traditionaliste et conservateur. L’article Pologne | Les dessous de la tentative de coup d’État de l’Européiste Tusk est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Centrafrique: trente ans après sa mort, l'héritage contrasté du dictateur Jean-Bedel Bokassa
items.description: La République centrafricaine se souvient ce 3 novembre des trente ans de la disparition de Jean-Bedel Bokassa. Trente ans après sa mort, la figure de l’ancien président, devenu empereur en 1977, continue de susciter la polémique dans le pays. Pour certains Centrafricains, Bokassa reste un bâtisseur, un dirigeant ambitieux et un pionnier du développement national. Pour d’autres, son règne demeure indissociable de la répression, des violences et des atteintes aux droits humains qui l'ont marqué. Au-delà des controverses, ce trentième anniversaire invite à regarder cette page de l’histoire avec lucidité et à s’interroger sur les leçons du passé.

items.title: AAUA bans signing-out ceremonies over security concerns
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The management of Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko (AAUA), Ondo State, has banned signing-out ceremonies and all related celebrations on campus over security concerns. The directive was contained in a circular issued by the Registrar, Dr Grace Olubunmi Babalola, dated October 30, 2026. According to the circular, the Vice-Chancellor, acting on behalf of the Senate, approved the ban in the interest of protecting lives and property within the university community. The management directed that no signing-out party, gathering, procession or other celebratory activity associated with the completion of academic programmes should be organised or held anywhere on campus until further notice. The directive takes immediate effect, with all students, particularly final-year students, urged to comply strictly. Deans, Heads of Departments, Heads of Units, security personnel and other relevant university officials have been directed to ensure strict enforcement and report any violation to the appropriate authorities. Babalola warned that students and other members of the university community who flout the directive would face disciplinary action in accordance with the institution’s extant laws and regulations. She added that cases involving suspected criminal conduct would be referred to law enforcement agencies for appropriate action. The Registrar urged members of the university community to cooperate with the management in maintaining a safe, peaceful and orderly campus environment, stressing that the suspension would remain in force until further notice. items.title: US votes today in midterms that could weaken Trump’s hold on Washington
items.description: Americans deliver their verdict on Donald Trump’s tumultuous second presidency on Tuesday in midterm elections that threaten to shatter his grip on Washington, with Democrats poised to seize the House and challenge for control of the Senate. Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump’s legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court justices and senior officials. The election amounts to a nationwide judgement on Trump, with the mood turning sharply against Republicans amid anger over soaring living costs and the war on Iran. All 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are at stake, along with governorships in 36 states. Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands. Trump returned to office last year promising to bring down prices, but inflation, tariffs and fuel costs inflated by the Middle East conflict have squeezed Americans. The 80-year-old’s approval rating has hovered near the low 30s. In the suburbs of Atlanta, Georgia, retired teacher Jane Callum, 77, was among Democrats canvassing for Senator Jon Ossoff who framed the race as a watershed moment for the country’s future. “I really feel an obligation to do everything that I possibly can to change the direction that our country is going in now, and put it more on the path to democracy and away from autocracy,” she told AFP . Economic discontent Republicans insist that Trump’s tax cuts and immigration crackdown will benefit Americans and they are portraying Democratic candidates as left-wing radicals. But in his final public campaign appearance Monday, Trump barely touched on the economy and spent most of the time in a rambling talk about his problem-plagued renovation of Washington’s Reflecting Pool. “This is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime,” he said, 26 minutes into the speech, before quickly returning to talking about renovations. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer branded it a “pathetic closing message.” Some Republican supporters remain confident. “We’re going to win. As a matter of fact, we’ve probably already won,” Texas military veteran Yvonne Clouser told AFP . But while Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority, the battlefield is extending into conservative states like Kansas, Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska. Democrats must also defend competitive seats, including in Michigan, where a bitter internal dispute saw congresswoman Haley Stevens endorse Republican Mike Rogers rather than the Democratic nominee, Abdul El-Sayed. Decision Desk HQ’s final forecast forecasted 241 House seats for Democrats against 194 for Republicans, and a narrower 52-48 Democratic Senate majority. Disputed results? Polls can underestimate one party’s support, and Republicans hope their voters turn out in force on Election Day. More than 57 million Americans had already voted early before Tuesday, indicating the high energy. The campaign has attracted more than $11 billion in political advertising, while billionaire Trump ally Elon Musk has poured hundreds of millions of dollars into Republican political efforts. As soon as polls close, concerns will mount over whether results will be accepted by the Republicans. Trump, who tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat, has repeatedly alleged widespread voter fraud and accused Democrats — with no evidence — of cheating. The Justice Department, run by a close Trump ally, has already sued to potentially block certification of Alaska’s Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses, although a court ruled against the effort on the eve of the election. And the Supreme Court rejected on Monday an emergency bid to force California to set aside the mail-in ballots of more than 20,000 people on the grounds they may not be American citizens. Trump, who will watch the midterms results at the White House on Tuesday night, signalled that if he does lose control of Congress he could simply defy Democrats. “I veto everything,” he told a podcast on Monday, although he said he might strike deals with Democrats eventually.

items.title: MAN convenes energy efficiency summit to boost manufacturing
items.description: By Yinka Kolawole The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) is set to convene a two-day energy efficiency summit in Lagos to address high energy costs, improve industrial competitiveness and promote investment in alternative power solutions. Speaking in Lagos, MAN President, Dr. Ifeanyi Okoye, said the summit would bring together industry leaders, policymakers, regulators, technology providers and financial institutions to develop practical solutions to Nigeria’s industrial energy challenges. The summit, scheduled for November 3 to 4, organised through MAN’s power and energy subsidiary, Manufacturers Power Development Company Ltd (MPDCL), in partnership with the German Development Agency (GIZ) and Nigerian Energy Support Programme (NESP), will hold at Legend Hotel Lagos Airport, Ikeja, Lagos. With the theme, “Innovative Energy for Cost-Effective Smart Manufacturing with Structured Financing,” the event will focus on industrial energy security, efficiency and cost reduction. Okoye said high electricity tariffs, unreliable grid supply, fuel price volatility and dependence on expensive self-generation remained major constraints on manufacturers, undermining competitiveness, fuelling inflation and limiting job creation and Nigeria’s ability to maximise opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). He said: “To build a resilient, self-sustaining economy, we must address these challenges through a multi-faceted approach by expanding our energy infrastructure, accelerating energy efficiency adoption, diversifying industrial energy sources, and forging deep public-private capital partnerships.” Also speaking, MAN Director-General, Segun Ajayi-Kadir, said previous summits had provided members with opportunities to engage solution providers, resulting in increased adoption of off-grid energy solutions by manufacturers. He said attracting investment was a major objective, noting that inadequate investment in the power sector and an unfavourable business environment had constrained capital inflows, particularly from foreign investors. items.title: Donald the Lame Duck? Trump will have other ideas if Republicans lose midterms
items.description: President Donald Trump’s second term has been a wild ride, but his last two years in power could be wilder still if Republicans lose control of Congress in Tuesday’s US midterm elections . From renewed military action against Iran to election challenges and fightbacks against Democratic investigations, Trump’s post-midterms playbook could involve disruption on all fronts. Analysts warn that Trump as a “lame duck” president could be the most vengeful Trump of all. “I’m skeptical that President Trump will go quiet into that good night,” Peter Loge, director of George Washington University’s School of Media and Public Affairs, told AFP . “There is nothing in history that says he will say ‘I’ve been beaten, my time is over’. Every time Trump has been backed into a corner, he has shouted more and come out fighting.” Vetoes and vengeance Trump has always viewed himself as a fighter. He has been clear he will take the same approach if Democrats win one or both chambers of Congress. “If we didn’t win, I veto everything” in any Democratic legislative agenda, Trump told the New York Post . A man walks past posters highlighting high food and gas prices and urging people to vote in Dallas, Texas, on November 2, 2026. —AFP The White House says it is also ready to fight back against whatever investigations — or impeachment proceedings — Democrats throw at them. “They’ll probably go after me, and I’ll go after them,” Trump said in a Time magazine interview. Trump could even direct the Justice Department to investigate Democrats who are probing him. Trump, who baselessly disputed his 2020 presidential election loss, could also interfere in the midterms by challenging counts or delaying the certification of disputed races. Iran Foreign policy is the one area in which lame-duck US presidents still have wide-ranging powers. Trump may renew large-scale military operations against Iran, although he appeared to indicate on the eve of the midterms that fresh talks could produce a deal. “I don’t think he wants his legacy to be a warmonger. He wants his legacy to have left America stronger,” Ryan Hass of the Brookings Institution told AFP . Speculation has swirled that Trump could fire Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth as the Iran war drags on — a familiar move for a president who never likes to take the blame. Ukraine, detente and trade Trump loves to think of himself as a master of peace deals and is likely to continue to push Ukraine to agree to a settlement with Russia . Fresh trilateral talks are set for next week. At the same time, Trump will continue to seek detente with the leaders he views as his great power equals — Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin . The three will potentially meet at a summit in China later this month. US President Donald Trump departs after delivering remarks at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on November 2, 2026 in Washington, DC. —Getty Images via AFP The US is also likely to continue its retrenchment from some of its NATO and other Western allies — and may even accelerate it, said Hass of the Brookings Institution. On trade, however, Trump would likely remain “unrelentingly active”, as shown by his recent hostility towards Canada, Hass said. Staying relevant for 2028? Trump loves being the centre of attention and is unlikely to relish the spotlight turning towards potential successors in the 2028 US presidential election. Trump — who hosted the reality television show The Apprentice — has been notably coy about backing either Vice President JD Vance or Secretary of State Marco Rubio for the top job. But Trump has largely stopped dropping hints at running for a constitutionally-barred third term. Allan Lichtman, a professor at American University and author of Great American Presidents: The Twelve Who Transformed the Nation , said Trump would certainly “keep the focus on himself by being the kingmaker.” Monuments to himself Like other people getting ready for retirement, Trump may choose to focus on home improvement. In his closing midterms speech, Trump barely mentioned policy and instead talked about his renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and other plans to beautify Washington. US President Donald leaves after delivering a speech marking the end of the midterm election campaign, in Washington, DC, on November 2, 2026. —AFP Trump has openly expressed a desire to stamp his own physical mark on Washington because he fears that others will not do it for him. “We have a lot of great things planned for Washington,” he said at the Reflecting Pool on Monday. Header image: US President Donald Trump stands, as he departs after delivering remarks ahead of the midterm elections at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, after being reopened following months of repairs, in Washington, DC, US on Nov 2, 2026. —Reuters
