items.title: Storage deficit
items.description: THE Strait of Hormuz closed on Feb 28, 2026. Within days, QatarEnergy declared force majeure . Pakistan, which sourced almost all its LNG from Qatar, asked Saudi Arabia to reroute crude through the Red Sea and released gas it had been holding back for weeks. There was no gas storage and very little oil storage to fall back on, because none had ever been built. The timing made it worse. Years earlier, Pakistan signed long-term LNG contracts. Then IMF-driven tariff changes made gas too expensive for industries running captive power plants, and they switched to solar. Demand fell just as the country was locked into more gas than it needed. The pipelines reached the capacity threshold and the authorities curtailed up to 350 mmcfd of domestic gas. Then the strait closed, Qatari cargoes were stranded, and the curtailed fields had to be switched back on within weeks. Too much gas, then too little, and no storage to manage either. This is not a new problem. Policymakers have known for decades that Pakistan needs oil and gas storage, but have done little about it. Gas storage works by pumping surplus gas into depleted reservoirs when demand is low and drawing it back out when supply runs short. As early as 2004, an ADB study examined 107 locations and recommended two depleted fields in Badin, and a 2022 study added a third. Exploration companies operate these fields and could convert them, but no commercial model has been settled. A guaranteed return for investors, the model that inflated power costs for two decades, would be a mistake. It paid for capacity whether used or not, and gave sponsors little reason to control costs. Competitive bidding works the other way: developers compete on the fee they charge to store and return gas, overrun risk stays with them, and the state only sets the terms. Feasibility tenders were issued in 2024 and again in 2026, a month before the strait closed. Even then, the first facility will cover only 11 to 12 days of consumption, against the month officials say is needed. Oil storage has failed for its own reasons. The main one is that no one is paid to hold it. Marketing companies must keep 20 days of cover, but prices are revised every fortnight, so extra stock risks a loss whenever prices fall, and the pricing formula does not recover the cost of tanks. Most companies stay near the minimum, and the state has never built a strategic reserve of its own. Pakistan needs oil and gas storage. The idea of letting foreign suppliers hold fuel in Pakistan was first floated in 2015. In 2023, the government approved it: suppliers could keep product in bonded storage without paying duty, pay only when they sold locally, and re-export freely. Not one supplier has used it — for three reasons. First, the rules require a foreign supplier to register a presence in Pakistan. Large traders are used to storing oil in places like Fujairah in the UAE or Singapore without opening an office there. Asking them to do so here adds cost and paperwork for little benefit. Second, nothing guarantees a supplier can take its oil back out. A future government facing a shortage could block exports, just when it would want to sell elsewhere. Third, five bodies have a say: customs, the regulator, the State Bank, and the commerce and petroleum ministries. Each writes its own rules, and no one makes them fit together. The current government has reopened the policy , an admission that it has attracted no investment. The strait showed that fuel stored in the Gulf can be cut off without warning. Fuel held in Pakistan by foreign suppliers, available for local sale, would give the country a cushion next time. The fix requires detail, not reinvention. The rules must state who can take part without a Pakistani company, how ownership changes when part of a tank is sold, how banks process those sales, and which single office settles disputes. Traders choose where to store oil based on how fast licences come and whether rules stay stable. Fujairah attracts traders not because its government built the tanks, but because it made storage simple and predictable. In both cases, the government need not spend its own money. Its job is to write clear rules, issue licences quickly, and honour its commitments. Pakistan has paid for the lack of storage twice this year, first with more gas than it could use, then with too little. The gas sites were identified over 20 years ago; the oil policy has existed for years. What has been missing is the will to follow through. Hormuz will not be the last disruption, and if storage is not ready before the next one, the cost will again fall on industry, on households, and on a treasury paying premium prices for emergency cargoes. The next closure will not wait for another feasibility study. The writer is a corporate lawyer working in the energy and infrastructure sector across the Middle East and Pakistan. Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

items.title: Ghana’s inflation projected to stay below 10% for next three to four years – Theo Acheampong
items.description: Economist and political risk specialist Dr Theo Acheampong says Ghana’s inflation is projected to remain below 10 per cent over the next three to four years. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, he pointed to the government’s medium-term fiscal projections. He said these indicated sustained single-digit inflation. “The forward projection for prices going forward into the next three to four years in the medium-term budget is all within the sub-10 %.” His comments followed a question about whether the government could guarantee price stability in 2027 and 2028. Dr Acheampong responded by referring to the budget framework and its economic expectations. His answer set out a projection, rather than an unconditional guarantee. “So, as I said, the government is going to present the 2027 Budget just next week.” He explained that the budget’s medium-term fiscal framework outlines expectations for growth, inflation, the size of the economy and fiscal balances. He also referred viewers to the previous budget projections, inviting them to check his account against the 2025 budget. For workers, he linked the inflation outlook to the value of future salary increases. He argued that a sustained single-digit inflation environment would leave them better off, on average, with wage increases of 9 or 10 per cent. “So basically, you’re still in a single-digit inflation environment, and to the extent that that still stays, and you can still offer workers 9%, you can still offer them 10%.” His argument rested on that inflation outlook holding. The projected rate of price increases would therefore determine how much benefit workers receive from subsequent pay adjustments.

items.title: Guilty of journalism
items.description: AS a journalist making a living solely in the industry, the challenging times confronting the profession are rarely far from one’s mind. Navel-gazing has become more than a side distraction in some ways. No wonder then that a new book on the industry by a stalwart, Mazhar Abbas, was on the must-read list. He has been active in both journalism and the trade union politics of media organisations; Abbas is someone who many in my generation look up to for being among the few who have been able to do both journalism and its politics proficiently and with integrity. None of this is insignificant. Since the proliferation of electronic media, union politics has rarely attracted journalists of stature. It is worth asking at this stage whether he is one of the last Mohicans. His latest book, Media Under the Shadow of Death, covers a wide range of issues — from the origins of the unions formed in the early years of a fledgling country to issues the industry grapples with today: censorship, violence against journalists, and the challenges of technology. For someone like myself who isn’t very well-versed in the history of union politics, the historical account in the early chapters of the book is a fascinating description of how the Sindh Union of Journalists and the Pakistan Federal Union of Journalists (PFUJ) came into being, and how journalists pushed back against the earlier undemocratic efforts of the state of Pakistan. Beyond the events themselves, discussions with people such as Roedad Khan also offer insight into the ruling elite’s thinking at the time and their attitudes towards democracy and press freedom. At the same time, this earlier period also reveals how far back some unfortunate trends go. Even then, journalists’ biases against one another, or in favour of one political stakeholder over another, allowed the state or government to take advantage. The principles of democracy or freedom of expression never proved bigger than personal likes or dislikes. He, too, quotes the famous story of journalists who went to Gen Ziaul Haq and asked him to delay the elections for fear of a PPP victory. In recent times, one has seen media groups attack each other at the behest of the powers that be. The second pattern, which seems to date back further than we realise, is the inability of media owners to match journalists in opposing the state’s suppressive methods; the latter’s decision to sign a code of conduct during the emergency imposed by Gen Pervez Musharraf is a case in point. But there are no sweeping judgements, as the financial pressures on the media owners and their limitations are also understood by the author. ‘Media Under the Shadow of Death’ documents the key challenges in Pakistani journalism. The strongest part is perhaps the account of the media under Musharraf. This is partly because it’s a recent period when Pakistan’s media flourished and expanded but also faced challenges, including increased violence against journalists as well as events such as the emergency. The latter happened when the author himself was an elected official of the PFUJ and was organising protests against the dictator’s actions. For those of us who were present at the time — in the trenches or on the sidelines — those were heady times. It seemed then that the political parties, lawyers’ organisations, journalists, and others could push back against a military dictator struggling to sustain his rule. No one thought this was simply a transitory moment; it seemed like a permanent change — though we have grown wiser since. But back then, it was a moment of great hope, and the PFUJ’s role was significant. Even now, reading about it brings a sense of satisfaction. As the author himself notes, it was perhaps the last time the federation acted with unity. However, he doesn’t go into the details of what happened later, or how the organisation not only split but has also become a shadow of its former self since then. With his intimate knowledge of union issues, Abbas could have provided an insight into the present mess in journalistic organisations and perhaps kick-started a debate on possible solutions. This omission is disappointing in some ways. The second strongest part of the book is the section where he discusses the killings of journalists, though given the number of case studies, not each case is tackled with an even hand. Some are detailed and some sketchy. However, the more high-profile the case, the more interesting the details — though they still leave one wanting more. This is especially true of cases such as Wali Babar’s , where Abbas provides the details of the deaths that followed the investigations of the journalist’s murder — police officers investigating the case, the prosecutor, and even witnesses were killed as the matter progressed. Similarly, the book details high-profile cases (Hayatullah Khan, Musa Khankhel, Arshad Sharif) as well as low-profile ones that may not have garnered much attention. Overall, the book is a resource compendium rather than a chronological or analytical account. There are historical accounts — a chapter on press laws and then one on the case studies of journalists’ killings. This also means the book’s tone is a wee uneven. Perhaps, as the author says at the outset, the book kept getting delayed because of the fast-changing events in the industry and the polity. This might also explain why the writing and editing needed a bit more work. One can only hope some of these issues are addressed in a second edition if there is to be one — for the information in the book is valuable and deserves to be read by those who still haven’t fallen out of love with this profession despite the filth we wallow in these days. The writer is a journalist. Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

items.title: An opening
items.description: AS the threat of renewed US-Israeli strikes on Iran lingers, a parallel diplomatic process — facilitated by Qatar and Pakistan — is attempting to avert a devastating return to hostilities. Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday to take part in indirect talks aimed at working out a deal, even as speculation of fresh attacks on Iran, following today’s midterm polls in America, continued. US President Donald Trump has not helped matters by toying with the idea of new attacks. The ice was broken late last month when US Vice-President J.D. Vance wrote a letter to Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei. Mr Vance reportedly prefers a diplomatic solution. Earlier, he had led his country’s delegation during April’s historic talks in Islamabad. The letter has been well received in Tehran, with Gen Rezaei calling its tone “positive”. Writing to the Iranian security chief was an intelligent move and has begun to show results. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said that if the US meets his country’s demands, the Strait of Hormuz could be reopened within two days. That outcome would be welcomed not only by the Gulf states and other regional countries but also by the international community at large, as states across the world have felt the impact of the strait’s closure and the attendant restrictions on trade and oil and gas flows. Mr Vance’s letter has reportedly asked for guarantees regarding Iran’s nuclear programme. On its part, Tehran wants an end to both the sanctions and the US blockade, as well as other concessions from America. Both sides must show flexibility if this push for peace is to succeed. Though the diplomatic progress is welcome, the process could be torpedoed if the US and Israel go ahead with their attack plans. Media reports indicate that Washington and Tel Aviv are prepared to resume hostilities after the midterms. However, US Democratic Senator Chris Murphy, who has been briefed on the plans, has described the latter as “insane” and likely to cause a “devastating escalation”. The Iranian Supreme Leader, on the other hand, has ordered his forces to retaliate to any attack “without geographical restriction”. It would be very irresponsible of the US and Israel to scuttle peace efforts and spark a potentially massive conflict. The regional states do not want war as they are aware of the destruction it will bring. It is time for more mature officials within the US administration, such as Mr Vance, to take the lead in ensuring that the peace process continues unimpeded, while warmongers in America and Israel must be isolated. If this brief opportunity for peace is wasted, sparking a wider conflict, the blame will rest squarely with the US president and the bloodthirsty Zionist regime. Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

items.title: 2026 WIC Wuzhen Summit opens with focus on open-source AI
items.description: The 2026 World Internet Conference (WIC) Wuzhen Summit opened on Tuesday in Wuzhen, east China's Zhejiang Province, bringing together governments, international organizations, businesses and academics from around the world. Under the theme "Open Source and Openness, Collaborative Development and Shared Benefits – Jointly Building a Community with a Shared Future in Cyberspace," this year's summit focuses on open-source AI, with discussions covering technological innovation, security governance, cultural exchanges and international cooperation. A highlight of the main forum is the AI Wuzhen Dialogue, which brings together leading global technology companies, executives from open-source large language model companies and AI scientists to explore ways to build a global open-source AI ecosystem. The summit also features 27 sub-forums covering topics such as cyberspace cooperation under the Global Governance Initiative, theories and policies in the digital and intelligent era, and robotics and embodied intelligence. The summit has also attracted international participation in its case collection and technology awards. The call for outstanding cases of jointly building a community with a shared future in cyberspace received 360 submissions from 80 countries and regions, 22 of which participated for the first time. Eleven cases were shortlisted. Meanwhile, the World Internet Conference Awards for Pioneering Science and Technology received more than 430 submissions from 43 countries and regions. Eighteen countries and regions submitted entries for the first time, while the number of international submissions increased by 21% year on year. A total of 20 projects received awards. Wang Jian, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, said he believes the WIC will continue to play an important role in China's AI development. As open source and openness are global in nature, he said, the Wuzhen Summit can help China contribute to global AI development. John Hoffman, CEO of GSMA Ltd., said the Wuzhen Summit provides a platform for sharing information and bringing together ideas on how to build an open internet accessible to all. He said this year's theme also reflects the summit's longstanding commitment to leaving no one behind and creating opportunities for the future of the world.

items.title: Le PLF 2027 poursuit son soutien à l'industrie du gaming et à la structuration du secteur
items.description: Le projet de loi de finances (PLF) de 2027 continuera de soutenir l'industrie des jeux vidéo (gaming) au Maroc, à travers des projets et des programmes qui visent à structurer le secteur et à conforter la place du Royaume en tant que pôle régional dans ce domaine, a indiqué lundi le ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et des Sports. Le PLF prévoit la poursuite de la création du « Rabat Gaming City », pour un coût global de 460 millions de dirhams, dont 160 millions déjà débloqués, dans l'objectif d'attirer les investissements et de garantir un environnement adapté aux studios de développement de jeux et aux entreprises émergentes, a précisé le ministère sur son site électronique. Il prévoit également la poursuite de la mise en oeuvre du programme « Gamification Lab », en partenariat avec CDG Invest, lequel mobilise une enveloppe budgétaire de 10 millions de dirhams durant la période 2027-2029, en vue de soutenir les solutions d’emploi des mécanismes de jeux électroniques développés par les studios marocains et de promouvoir les compétences dans les métiers du numérique. Ces initiatives s'inscrivent dans le cadre des efforts visant à développer le gaming au Maroc, à encourager l'innovation et l'investissement et à favoriser la création de nouvelles opportunités pour les jeunes et les entreprises marocaines. items.title: Govt seeks PPP, MQM nominees for electoral reforms panel
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Taking ownership of an initiative to bring all parliamentary parties, including the opposition, to the negotiating table on electoral reforms, the government on Monday formally appr­oached its allies to join the proposed Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms (PCER). The government contacted its key allies, the PPP and the MQM, seeking nominations for their representatives on the proposed committee. The PPP has submitted the names of its legislators for the PCER. However, the names have not yet been made public. Federal Minister for Par­liamentary Affairs Tar­iq Fazal Chaudhry wrote separate letters to the chief whips of the PPP and MQM in the National Ass­embly, Ijaz Jakhrani and Aminul Haq, respectively, seeking nominations for the committee. Talking to Dawn , Mr Chaudhry said National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq had received the names from the PPP. However, he said the government would announce the names of all committee members at a later stage. He said the ruling PML-N would have nine members, while the PPP would have five and the MQM one. Explaining the formula for representation of parliamentary parties on the committee, the minister said one member would be allocated for every 16 members of the National Assembly. He said that, under the agreed criteria, smaller parties allied with the ruling coalition did not qualify for representation on the committee. The PML-N had therefore decided to allocate one seat each to its smaller allies, including the Balochistan Awami Party (BAP) and Pakistan Muslim League-Zia (PML-Z), from its own quota of nine seats. Asked whether the government would also directly approach the opposition to seek nominations for the committee, Mr Chaudhry said the PPP had already contacted opposition parties and that they were now required to submit the names of their representatives directly to the National Assembly speaker. The parliamentary affairs minister clarified that the initiative to form the committee had been taken by Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, not the PPP. He said he would begin meeting parliamentary leaders of all parties from today (Tuesday) to obtain nominations for the electoral reforms committee. Mr Chaudhry said there was no reason to believe that the PML-N-led government would not complete its five-year constitutional term. He added that the PPP had met opposition leaders at the initiative of the National Assembly speaker. “The PPP can only meet opposition leaders as a political move, but the party has no mandate to do anything else,” he said. Responding to a question, Mr Chaudhry acknowledged that the PPP was creating difficulties for the government in legislative business. “The PPP is pinching us in making legislation, but the party cannot keep itself away from the system,” he said. He insisted that the opposition should join the parliamentary committee, saying the initiative would open the door to consultations on other important national issues. Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

items.title: Taliban govt voices concern over US plans for deportation
items.description: KABUL: Afghanistan’s Taliban authorities voiced concern on Monday over reported plans by Washington to deport scores of Afghan immigrants to Pakistan with the aim of their eventual return to their home country. More than 150 Afghans in the United States would be deported via Pakistan to Afghanistan, including relatives of those who assisted US forces before their 2021 withdrawal, according to US media reports and an advocacy group. “The Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan expresses its serious concern over reports that the United States intends to deport some Afghan refugees to Pakistan who have not yet been able to obtain legal residency documents in that country,” foreign ministry spokesman Abdul Qahar Balkhi said in a statement. Advocacy groups have warned that the removal of former allies and their families could endanger their lives. After regaining power, Taliban authorities announced a general amnesty for Afghans who worked with Western-backed forces and governments and have repeated promises this year that their former foes could safely return home. However, the United Nations has recorded reports of extrajudicial killings, detentions and abuses. President Donald Trump’s administration last year issued travel bans for a number of countries, including Afghanistan, as part of a broad immigration crackdown. His administration sought to end deportation protections for Afghans, some of whom were granted special immigrant visas following the 2021 takeover by Taliban authorities. Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

items.title: Currency outside banks rises 104% in 3 yrs — CBN
items.description: •Demand deposits climb 71% •Analysts highlight cash dependence, financial inclusion challenges By Peter Egwuatu Currency held outside the banking system by Nigerians rose by 103.8 per cent to N4.923 trillion in September 2026 from N2.416 trillion in September 2023, highlighting the persistent demand for physical cash despite the expansion of electronic payment channels in the country. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Money and Credit Statistics, also showed that currency outside banks increased by 10.3 per cent year-on-year from N4.465 trillion in September 2025 to N4.923 trillion in September 2026. The figures indicate that cash held outside the banking system has more than doubled in three years, reflecting the scale of currency demand within the economy and the challenges facing efforts to deepen the use of formal banking and electronic payment systems. A breakdown of the data showed that currency outside banks increased by 66.2 per cent from N2.416 trillion in September 2023 to N4.016 trillion in September 2024. The figure subsequently rose to N4.465 trillion in September 2025, an increase of 11.2 per cent from the corresponding period in 2024, before climbing further to N4.923 trillion in September 2026. According to analysts, the latest increase indicates that the preference for cash transactions remains significant, notwithstanding the growing adoption of mobile banking, electronic transfers, point-of-sale terminals and other digital payment platforms. Demand deposits rise 71% Meanwhile, demand deposits in the banking system increased by 70.8 per cent to N39.124 trillion in September 2026 from N22.903 trillion in September 2023. The CBN data showed that demand deposits rose to N31.842 trillion in September 2024, representing an increase of 39.0 per cent against the corresponding period in 2023. The figure climbed further to N34.642 trillion in September 2025, an increase of 8.8 per cent year-on-year, before rising to N39.124 trillion in September 2026, representing a 12.9 per cent increase over September 2025. The growth in demand deposits indicates an expansion in funds held in bank accounts that are generally accessible for payments and withdrawals on demand. Reacting to this data, Clifford Egbomeade, Economic and Communications expert, said: “The simultaneous increase in demand deposits and currency outside banks points to the coexistence of formal banking balances and substantial demand for physical cash in Nigeria’s payment system. ‘‘However, the two indicators measure different components of monetary activity. Demand deposits represent bank-account balances, while currency outside banks represents cash held outside the banking system. ‘‘Their growth rates alone do not establish how much of the increase in cash holdings is attributable to economic growth, inflation, informal transactions or changes in payment preferences.” Vanguard News The post Currency outside banks rises 104% in 3 yrs — CBN appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Traque des chefs terroristes au Burkina Faso: Après Sangaré Barry et Karim Torodo, le sinistre Saïdou Diallo abattu dans la Boucle du Mouhoun
items.description: Dans une offensive d'envergure menée dans la matinée du jeudi 29 octobre 2026 dans la province du Sourou, les Forces spéciales antiterroristes de campagne (FORSATEC) ont neutralisé l'un des chefs terroristes les plus craints de la région : Saïdou Diallo, dit Djabiri Mangan ou « le Borgne ». Selon des informations exclusives rapportées par l'Agence d’information du Burkina (AIB) auprès de sources sécuritaires, l'assaut lancé au cœur de la forêt de Konga, dans la commune de Gomboro, a permis de démanteler plusieurs repaires du Groupe de soutien à l'islam et aux musulmans (GSIM) et de récupérer un arsenal logistique conséquent. Outre ses attaques contre les forces de défense et les civils, cet individu de 47 ans constituait la cheville ouvrière du ravitaillement logistique et du trafic de bétail volé dans les provinces du Sourou et du Yatenga. L'étau continue de se resserrer inexorablement autour des bastions terroristes. D'après les éléments révélés par l'Agence d'information du Burkina (AIB), les forces combattantes ont déclenché, dans la matinée du jeudi 29 octobre 2026, une opération d'envergure ciblant des éléments affiliés au Groupe de soutien à l'islam et aux musulmans (GSIM) retranchés dans les profondeurs de la forêt de Konga, située dans la commune de Gomboro (province du Sourou). Menée avec précision par une unité des Forces spéciales antiterroristes de campagne (FORSATEC), cette intervention coordonnée a abouti à la neutralisation de plusieurs assaillants et au démantèlement complet de plusieurs bases ennemies. Au premier rang des terroristes abattus figure une prise majeure : Saïdou Diallo, plus connu sous le nom de guerre de Djabiri Mangan, alias « le Borgne ». Âgé d'environ quarante-sept ans et natif de Toaga, dans la commune de Tougan, cet individu servait d’adjoint au chef de la base terroriste de Konga/Gomboro. Les investigations sécuritaires relayées par l'AIB mettent en lumière le rôle stratégique et central qu'il occupait au sein de la nébuleuse. Véritable pivot de l'approvisionnement des bandes armées, Saïdou Diallo orchestrait l’écoulement du cheptel pillé aux éleveurs et populations locales afin de financer les cellules djihadistes, tout en assurant l'acheminement de treillis, tenues et accessoires militaires à destination des maquis. Son parcours sanguinaire a lourdement endeuillé le septentrion et l'ouest du pays : l'homme a personnellement pris part à de multiples assauts contre les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), les Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP) ainsi que contre des civils désarmés, semant la terreur dans les communes de Kiembara, Lankoué, Tougan et Gomboro dans le Sourou, mais aussi à Thiou et Tangaye dans la province voisine du Yatenga. Au terme des affrontements, les unités au sol ont mis la main sur une importante prise logistique. Les militaires ont notamment récupéré des armes de guerre, de nombreux engins roulants, des cargaisons de vivres ainsi que des stocks de produits pharmaceutiques destinés à soigner les combattants blessés. En éliminant cet adjoint opérationnel et logisticien clé, l'armée inflige un coup sévère aux capacités de projection et de survie des groupes armés sévissant dans le Sourou et le Yatenga, tout en privant ces réseaux d’une ressource financière issue de la prédation pastorale. Ce succès s'inscrit dans une série de revers majeurs infligés ces derniers mois aux figures de proue du terrorisme au Burkina Faso. L'élimination de Diallo fait écho à celle opérée le 25 juillet 2026 dans la forêt de Kinséré (Barani, province de Koosin), où quinze assaillants avaient été mis hors de combat, parmi lesquels leur chef Sangaré Barry Manga (32 ans), cadre actif depuis 2018. Plus tôt dans l’année, le 16 janvier 2026, une embuscade tendue entre Koogo et Menè (Koulpélogo) avait coûté la vie à cinquante-sept criminels, neutralisant au passage Karim Torodo, alias Abdoul Bachirou, émir du GSIM pour le Nakambé, dont la tête avait été mise à prix à 175 millions de FCFA en juin 2023. Par cette action résolue dans le Sourou, les forces combattantes confirment l'intensification de la reconquête territoriale et la neutralisation systématique de la chaîne de commandement ennemie. L’article Traque des chefs terroristes au Burkina Faso: Après Sangaré Barry et Karim Torodo, le sinistre Saïdou Diallo abattu dans la Boucle du Mouhoun est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Rebondissement judiciaire : À peine libérés sous caution de 20 millions de FCFA, l’ancien ministre Lionel Bilgo de retour en cellule
items.description: Un répit de courte durée pour l'ancien ministre de l’Éducation nationale, Lionel Bilgo, et son co-prévenu, Vincent De Paul Kaboré. Alors qu'ils avaient obtenu, le mercredi 14 octobre 2026 devant la Cour d'appel de Bobo-Dioulasso, une liberté provisoire assortie d’une caution de 20 millions de FCFA chacun dans un volet de blanchiment de capitaux, les deux hommes ont été réincarcérés le lundi 19 octobre 2026. Selon des informations rapportées par l'Agence d’information du Burkina (AIB) auprès du procureur du Faso près le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Bobo-Dioulasso, cette remise en détention découle d’une procédure distincte relative à la promotion immobilière, pour laquelle le mandat de dépôt restait pleinement exécutoire. Une nouvelle audience a été fixée au 16 novembre 2026. La parenthèse hors des cellules aura été particulièrement brève pour l’ancien membre du gouvernement. Incarcérés depuis le 28 août 2026 dans la capitale économique burkinabè, l’ancien ministre de l’Éducation nationale, Lionel Bilgo, et son co-prévenu, Vincent De Paul Kaboré, avaient entrevu une première éclaircie judiciaire le mercredi 14 octobre 2026. Ce jour-là, la Cour d'appel de Bobo-Dioulasso leur accordait une mise en liberté provisoire, conditionnée au versement d'une caution de 20 millions de francs CFA pour chacun d'eux. Cependant, moins de cinq jours après cette décision, les deux prévenus ont été reconduits en prison dès le lundi 19 octobre 2026. Cette réincarcération expéditive s'explique par la coexistence de deux volets pénaux distincts. D'après les éléments judiciaires recueillis par l’Agence d’information du Burkina (AIB), les deux mis en cause sont poursuivis pour plusieurs infractions financières et économiques articulées autour de deux dossiers majeurs : le blanchiment de capitaux d'une part, et des infractions liées à la promotion immobilière d'autre part. Or, l'arrêt rendu le 14 octobre par la Cour d'appel ne statuait strictement que sur le mandat de dépôt décerné dans le cadre des faits de blanchiment de capitaux. Lors de l'audience tenue le lundi 19 octobre 2026, le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Bobo-Dioulasso a examiné le volet foncier et immobilier de l'affaire. À la barre, le procureur du Faso a souligné avec fermeté que la décision de mise en liberté provisoire intervenue la semaine précédente ne purgeait en rien le mandat d'arrêt émis au titre de la procédure sur la promotion immobilière. Requérant le maintien en détention des deux prévenus pour préserver le cours des poursuites, le parquet a été intégralement suivi dans ses réquisitions par le tribunal, qui a ordonné leur réintégration immédiate derrière les barreaux. Ce revirement maintient les deux prévenus en détention préventive dans l'attente du prochain round d'audience. Selon les précisions obtenues par l'AIB auprès des autorités judiciaires locales, le dossier a été renvoyé au 16 novembre 2026 devant le Tribunal de grande instance de Bobo-Dioulasso. Cette comparution constituera une étape charnière pour la défense de Lionel Bilgo et de Vincent De Paul Kaboré, qui devront répondre des multiples infractions qui leur sont reprochées dans ce dossier immobilier complexe. items.title: Women in Politics: Nigeria’s political structure not built for women — Adeola Azeez
items.description: By Ebunoluwa Sessou As Nigeria prepares for another general election in 2027, the question of women’s participation in politics and access to elective offices remains a subject for debate. Read Also: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters Adeola Azeez, a daughter of the late Afenifere leader, Pa Ayo Adebanjo and one of the Founders of Women in Management, Business & Public Service, WIMBIZ, a founding member of Women in Politics (WIMPol) and a former Deputy Country Representative, Nigeria, of Deutsch e-Bank; was recently declared winner at the Ijebu Central Federal Consistency primary election on the platform of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Ogun State. In this interview, she speaks on her experience contesting for the House of Representatives, the challenges of securing a party ticket, the influence of party structures on women’s political ambitions and her determination to contest again in 2027. She also discusses the need for women who have secured elective positions to support aspiring female politicians and explains why she believes women must remain committed to political participation despite the barriers they face. Excerpts: You transitioned from the corporate world to politics after your retirement in 2020. What informed that decision? I have always believed in the importance of women’s participation in leadership. By the time I retired in 2020, I had prepared myself for a career in politics. From 2013, I knew that politics was something I wanted to pursue, so I began preparing for it. I eventually contested for the House of Representatives in 2023 to represent Ogbomoso Central Federal Constituency. I approached the contest with the same seriousness, preparation and determination as any other candidate. What were the major challenges you encountered as a woman contesting for political office? The challenges women face in politics are well known. They include political violence, limited access to funding and other barriers. Interestingly, funding was not a major challenge for me because of my corporate experience and the relationships I had built over the years. Having supported, mentored and nurtured women in business, I had established a strong network of sponsors and supporters. My reputation also helped me attract people who believed in my ambition. However, the major challenge was the political structure itself. Nigeria’s political system is not structured to accommodate women adequately. Despite your corporate experience, network and supporters, you did not secure your party’s ticket in 2023. What went wrong? I believe the challenge was the party structure and the people who control access to political opportunities. I had expected that my pedigree, experience and contributions to society would count for something. I did my research, reached out to my constituency and carried out the necessary groundwork. I wanted to become a symbol of a new chapter for women in Nigerian politics. I believed that if more women with experience, credibility and the capacity to lead could successfully navigate the political system, it would encourage others to participate. Unfortunately, I did not secure the ticket. You have said that funding was not a major problem for you. Did you face pressure to engage in money politics? I was determined not to engage in money politics or buy votes. I believed doing so would compromise my principles and disappoint the people who had supported me, including my family. I wanted to run a campaign based on my record, ideas, engagement with the people and the support I had earned. Although I had supporters and people who believed in my ambition, that was not enough to overcome the challenges within the party structure. There was also the question of whether I would play politics in the same way as others. I believe women should be able to participate in politics without being expected to compromise their values to gain acceptance. Do you think the political system discriminates against women who refuse to play by the established rules? The political structure presents significant challenges for women. My experience made me realise that having the qualifications, resources, networks and willingness to serve does not automatically translate into securing a party ticket. Women must navigate party structures and the interests of those who control them. This is one of the reasons we must continue to examine the barriers preventing women from participating fully in politics. We need a system that recognises competence and allows women to compete meaningfully for elective positions. What lessons did you learn from your 2023 electoral experience? I learnt that political participation requires persistence. I did not give up after 2023 and I remained committed to my constituency. Although I did not secure the ticket, the experience gave me visibility. People in my constituency came to know me, my ambition and the kind of campaign I ran. I believe political participation should not begin and end with winning an election. There is a responsibility to continue contributing to the development of the people, regardless of whether one occupies political office or not. What are your plans for the 2027 general election? I am preparing to contest again in 2027, this time on a different party platform. My experience in 2023 has strengthened my resolve. The people in my constituency know me, and I believe my previous campaign helped establish a relationship with them. I am determined to continue and look forward to the next election. Beyond your political ambition, what have you done to improve the lives of people in your constituency? I have continued to support initiatives that respond to the needs of the people. This year, I facilitated the establishment of a technology hub and supported a back-to-school initiative. These projects were funded with the support of my partners. For me, leadership is about impact. Even when you are not holding an elected office, you can still contribute to the development of your community. I want people to understand that political aspirations should not prevent anyone from serving. We must continue to identify needs and provide support where possible. Some women who have secured elective offices are criticised for not doing enough to support other aspiring female politicians. Do you share this concern? There is still a lot of work to be done. We have women who are interested in politics, women who are preparing themselves and women who have the capacity to lead. The challenge is creating an environment where they can participate meaningfully. One concern is that some women who eventually get elected may not use their positions and influence to create opportunities for other women. When women get into the Senate or the House of Representatives, they should remember the challenges they faced on their way to those positions. They should use their influence to support other women who are trying to enter the political space. Women’s political representation should not be about individual achievement alone but creating a pathway for others. What practical steps should political parties take to improve women’s representation? We must move beyond simply encouraging women to participate, we must address the structural barriers that prevent them from securing party tickets and winning elections. Women need support, access to political opportunities and a system that recognises their capacity to lead. We must also build stronger networks of women who are willing to support one another. Those who have the resources, experience and influence should help aspiring female politicians navigate the political process. There are women who are prepared to serve, but we must create an environment where their preparation and capacity can translate into meaningful political participation. What is your message to women who are discouraged by the challenges of Nigerian politics? Women must not give up. We are trying, and we are rebuilding. There is a growing pool of women who are interested in politics and willing to contribute to national development. However, the fact that many women are trying but are not making significant progress in representation shows that there is still much work to do. We must continue to organise, support one another, build networks and challenge the barriers within the political system. I remain committed to that cause, and I believe women must keep pushing for their place in leadership. Vanguard News The post Women in Politics: Nigeria’s political structure not built for women — Adeola Azeez appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Plaintes des nouveaux bacheliers de la diaspora sur les réseaux sociaux: « Qu’ils repartent d’où ils viennent ! », prévient le Pr Adjima Thiombiano
items.description: La traditionnelle cérémonie de montée des couleurs nationales à l’immeuble de l’éducation, tenue ce lundi 2 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, a servi de tribune à une mise au point retentissante. Face aux propos jugés malveillants tenus sur les réseaux sociaux par de nouveaux bacheliers de la diaspora, le ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l’Innovation, le Pr Adjima Thiombiano, a vivement réagi. Tout en réaffirmant la fierté d'être burkinabè et l'engagement des autorités à valoriser l'université nationale à travers le Pacte NEKRÉ, le membre du gouvernement a prévenu qu'aucun dénigrement ni aucune perturbation du milieu universitaire ne seraient tolérés : « S'ils viennent pour dénigrer ce pays, ils trouveront tous les Burkinabè sur leur chemin. » Le message du mois s'est mué en un vibrant plaidoyer patriotique et d'autorité. Réunis ce lundi matin sur l'esplanade de l'immeuble de l'éducation, les personnels du Ministère de l’Enseignement Supérieur, de la Recherche et de l’Innovation (MESRI) ainsi que du Ministère de l’Enseignement de Base, de l’Alphabétisation et de la Promotion des Langues nationales participaient à la rituelle montée du drapeau. Présidée conjointement par les ministres Pr Adjima Thiombiano et Jacques Sosthène Dingara, la rencontre a été marquée par une réaction ferme du chef du département de l'enseignement supérieur face aux sorties controversées de récents bacheliers issus de la diaspora sur les plateformes numériques. Le ministre n'a pas mâché ses mots à l'endroit de ceux qui critiquent la terre natale. « Si le Burkina ne leur convient pas, qu’ils repartent d’où ils viennent… nous sommes très fiers d’être des Burkinabè et nous nous battons toujours pour que le Burkina soit meilleur » , a martelé le Pr Adjima Thiombiano. Saluant la démarche noble de tout enfant revenant étudier dans son pays d'origine avec de bonnes intentions, le ministre a toutefois tracé une ligne rouge infranchissable : tout comportement hostile ou dénigrant trouvera l'ensemble de la communauté nationale dressée en rempart. « Il n’y aura pas de place pour ces enfants égarés dans nos campus. Nous n’allons pas tolérer que tout ce que nous avons construit en quatre années soit battu en brèche » , a-t-il fermement averti. Cette mise en garde s'adosse à un vaste chantier institutionnel de refondation. Le Pr Thiombiano a rappelé le lancement officiel, intervenu le 17 octobre 2026 à Kaya, du Pacte NEKRÉ, conçu pour assurer la cohérence intégrale de la chaîne éducative, de la maternelle aux cycles universitaires. Appelant l'ensemble de la communauté éducative à faire bloc contre les attitudes « frisant la révolte », le ministre a insisté sur la nécessité de préserver le climat d'études et de redonner à l'université burkinabè ses lettres de noblesse, dans la droite ligne de la dynamique impulsée par les plus hautes autorités du pays. L’allocution ministérielle s'est également voulue un hommage appuyé aux défenseurs de la patrie. Au lendemain de la célébration du 66ᵉ anniversaire des Forces armées nationales, le 1ᵉʳ novembre 2026, le Pr Adjima Thiombiano a adressé ses vœux et exprimé sa profonde reconnaissance aux hommes et aux femmes engagés sur le théâtre des opérations. Une gratitude réitérée pour le sacrifice consenti au quotidien afin de maintenir le pays debout et permettre aux institutions républicaines de poursuivre leur mission éducatrice et souveraine. items.title: Chinese opera singer finds his stage on Italy's streets
items.description: Italy is known as the birthplace of opera. Home to some of opera’s greatest stars, including Luciano Pavarotti, Andrea Bocelli and Cecilia Bartoli, to name a few, the gift of opera singing is mostly preserved for grand stages and is usually not part of a sightseeing itinerary. However, for 25-year-old Zou Yanjie, public spaces have become his very own stage. "First of all, I want to get opera out of the theater and to get to the general public," he told CGTN in an interview. A talented young singer from southeast China's Jiangxi Province, now based in Milan, Zou is taking the art form into open spaces, including tourist attractions, squares and streets, where anyone can listen. Alongside Italian and French opera excerpts, he sings beautiful Chinese melodies, hoping to introduce local audiences to music they might never otherwise hear. Suddenly, a stroll down a street can become an unexpected and cheeky introduction to Chinese music. His journey began long before the street performances and online attention. Drawn to singing as a child, he started professional training in his teens and received systematic vocal training in China. "As I learned more about opera, I fell in love with the art," he said. "I traveled to Italy, the birthplace of opera, to refine my singing skills. Then I started trying to improvise on the street, which became a very special experience in my artistic path." He is still primarily a student and fits performances around his vocal studies. The idea of performing outdoors came from watching Italian musicians perform in the streets. "I thought to myself that I could also bring Chinese vocal works to this open-air stage, which led to the idea of impromptu street performances." Doing it took some courage and required him to step outside of his comfort zone. "I did get nervous and shy at first," he said. "But I keep reminding myself that I'm here to share the music." Once he began singing and concentrated on the music, the nerves gradually eased. Sharing something he loved became more important than worrying about being watched. The response has been warm, with passersby watching in awe, recording videos and applauding. "When I perform Chinese works, locals are filled with curiosity; many approach me to thank me for bringing such beautiful music," he said. Questions about Chinese music, traditions and everyday life often follow. Some listeners tell him they hope to visit China and experience the culture for themselves. Those street encounters now reach far beyond Italy. His videos have attracted millions of views across social media. "I couldn't have expected this much attention," he said. He began recording simply to document his performances. The attention has also brought opportunities, including invitations to local cultural events and collaborations with musicians blending Western opera and Chinese music. Still, Zou sees his performances and videos as a small window into Chinese culture rather than proof of some sweeping achievement. "I believe every little display has value," he said. Living alone in Italy, with his family back in China, has brought challenges too. Language and cultural differences took time to navigate. He now manages basic everyday conversations in Italian and sings in Italian and French as well as Chinese. "My family is very supportive," he said. "Seeing the videos online, they feel proud of me and hope I will persist in my dreams, spreading Chinese art abroad. At the same time, they often remind me to look after myself here." Zou hopes to take his street performances to more European cities and eventually beyond. For now, he wants to keep improving his voice, and whether someone listens in a public square or watches on a phone, his hope is the same, to be a bridge between Chinese and Western art. "My long-term aspiration is to enable more listeners around the world to hear and appreciate the beauty of Chinese vocal music," he said.

items.title: Récit bouleversant d’un sauvetage impuissant face au brasier sur l’axe Diébougou–Ouagadougou: Le père et son fils sauvés des flammes in extremis, la grand-mère périt calcinée
items.description: Ce dimanche 1ᵉʳ novembre 2026, la route a encore frappé en plein cœur, transformant un simple voyage en un cauchemar inoubliable. Vers le village de Foudjan, après Oronkoa, une voiture a quitté la voie, a cogné un arbre et a pris feu avec trois personnes piégées à l'intérieur : un père, son fils et sa vieille maman. Témoin direct du choc alors qu’il partait pour une formation, Rayiwindin Romba a foncé vers les flammes avec d'autres passagers pour sauver ces vies humaines. À mains nues et avec des pierres, ils ont réussi à faire sortir le chauffeur et le petit garçon. Mais devant la carcasse pliée et la violence du feu qui dévorait tout, ils ont dû lâcher les bras de la grand-mère et la regarder mourir sans rien pouvoir faire de plus. Un récit douloureux qui serre la gorge. Ce dimanche 1ᵉʳ novembre 2026, monsieur Rayiwindin Romba roule sur l'axe Diébougou–Ouagadougou avec des collègues pour aller suivre une formation d'enseignants organisé par le MEBAPLN en vue de renforcer les capacités pédagogiques des acteurs éducatifs. Tout se passe bien jusqu'à l'entrée du village de Foudjan. Soudain, sous leurs yeux, une voiture quitte la route, part dans les hautes herbes et s'écrase violemment contre un gros arbre. Quelques secondes plus tard, la fumée monte et les premières flammes apparaissent. Les témoins crient de peur et s'arrêtent aussitôt. Impossible de continuer son chemin sans réagir : des personnes sont enfermées dans ce piège de fer en feu. Rayiwindin et ses compagnons courent de toutes leurs forces vers le véhicule. En arrivant tout près de la voiture, la chaleur brûle déjà le visage. À l'intérieur, trois personnes crient et bougent encore : le chauffeur, son petit garçon et sa propre mère, assise devant. Le choc a tellement tordu la voiture que les portes refusent de s'ouvrir. Heureusement, la vitre du chauffeur est restée ouverte. En vitesse, les sauveteurs enlèvent sa ceinture et le tirent par la petite fenêtre pour le sortir du brasier. Un car de la compagnie TSR arrive avec trois extincteurs pour essayer d'éteindre le feu. Mais la poudre ne suffit pas et les flammes deviennent encore plus grandes. Il ne faut pas perdre une seconde. Avec de grosses pierres ramassées par terre, les volontaires frappent fort, cassent les autres vitres et réussissent à attraper l'enfant. Le petit garçon est sauvé à son tour des griffes de la mort. L'horreur : Regarder mourir une maman dans les flammes Il ne reste plus que la grand-mère. Mais le choc contre l'arbre a totalement écrasé l'avant du véhicule. Ses jambes et son corps sont coincés sous le métal tordu. Par la vitre cassée, Rayiwindin Romba et ses camarades passent leurs bras à l'intérieur malgré la chaleur qui pique les yeux et la gorge. Ils attrapent sa tête, entourent ses épaules de leurs mains et tirent de toutes leurs forces. Mais la voiture refuse de la lâcher. Autour d'eux, le feu crépite et rugit. La chaleur devient insupportable : le casque de moto de Rayiwindin commence à brûler, son sac et sa moto risquent de prendre feu. Les sauveteurs n'ont plus d'air et leurs peaux commencent à chauffer dangereusement. Avec la mort dans l'âme et des larmes plein les yeux, ils sont obligés de lâcher prise et de reculer d'un pas. Les mains vides et le cœur brisé, ils assistent, sans rien pouvoir faire, à la mort de cette maman consumée par les flammes jusqu'à devenir de la cendre. « Yako maman… Que ton âme repose en paix » , a écrit avec douleur Rayiwindin Romba sur sa page Facebook. Encore sous le choc, cet homme de courage rappelle que les affaires brûlées ne sont rien à côté d'une vie humaine : « Le matériel est peu de choses face à la vie humaine » . Pour lui, devant un accident, personne ne doit rester assis à regarder comme au spectacle, car chaque seconde compte pour sauver un frère ou une sœur. En pleurant le départ de cette mère partie trop tôt, il invite chacun à la prière pour la guérison du fils et du petit-fils, et lance un cri du cœur à tous les conducteurs : faites attention à la vitesse, ne buvez jamais d'alcool avant de conduire et arrêtez-vous dès que le sommeil commence à fermer vos yeux. L’article Récit bouleversant d'un sauvetage impuissant face au brasier sur l'axe Diébougou–Ouagadougou: Le père et son fils sauvés des flammes in extremis, la grand-mère périt calcinée est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Sindh govt moves to demolish fire-ravaged Gul Plaza building
items.description: KARACHI: The Sindh government has begun implementing its decision to demolish the charred, structurally damaged Gul Plaza building and has invited bids from interested firms to demolish the fire-ravaged commercial complex. According to an official announcement, the Sindh Building Control Authority will supervise the demolition process, for which technical and financial proposals have been invited separately. Interested firms can submit their bids by Nov 20. The move follows recommendations by a technical committee, which submitted its report in January, declaring the damaged structure unfit for use and recommending its demolition. Located on M.A. Jinnah Road, Gul Plaza was one of the city’s major commercial centres for decades. Built on an area of 8,128 square yards, the shopping complex housed hundreds of businesses and served as a popular shopping destination. The building was devastated by a massive fire that broke out in January 2026. The firefighting operation continued for several days before the blaze was finally brought under control. The tragic incident claimed 72 lives and destroyed more than 1,153 shops, leaving thousands of traders facing massive financial losses. The scale of the tragedy also raised serious questions about fire safety arrangements, emergency response mechanisms and safety standards in the city’s densely populated commercial buildings. “Following the incident, a technical committee examined the damaged structure and recommended its demolition, citing the extent of the destruction,” an official said, explaining the reason for the latest move. Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

items.title: Centre mulls reversing Fata merger, says Fazl
items.description: PESHAWAR: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rahman on Monday alleged that the federal government was considering reversing the merger of Fata with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. “The merger of Fata with this province is being proposed to be revoked. High-level government men have directly told me that the decision to merge the region was a mistake. Those running this system have told me directly that they want to revoke the merger and restore its previous status,” Mr Fazl told a convention of digital media workers of his party’s merged areas chapter here. The JUI-F chief said the merged districts had, unfortunately, been made a laboratory. He added that as a son of the soil and a Pakistani, he had questions that needed to be answered by the government. Complains character assassination drives launched against him Mr Fazl, however, said instead of addressing those concerns, character assassination campaigns were launched against him. “We’re aware of whose behest Fata was merged with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and whose interests would be served by bringing the area back under federal control,” he said. The JUI-F chief said that at the time of the merger when the region’s political and constitutional future was being decided, he had expressed serious reservations, maintaining that conditions were not suitable. He, however, said that even 10 years after the merger, the administrative system of the settled areas had yet to be established in the region. Mr Fazl said there was still no patwari in the region and the government had failed to establish a land revenue system. He added that a proper police system couldn’t be set up in the province, while the deputy commissioners posted to the region were baffled and helpless, wondering what to do. “Today, the issue is not political or constitutional. It’s about Fata’s resources and its economy,” he said. The JUI-F chief said he had been maintaining for a long time that the issue concerning erstwhile Fata was linked to its mineral resources. He, however, said he was not opposed to foreign investment by multinational companies. Mr Fazl said Chinese investors, who were making huge investments under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), were unhappy as hurdles were being created in the way of their investments. “If China is not happy about its investment here, other countries, too, would not invest,” he said. The JUI-F chief said the US was replacing the Chinese. He said the governor’s rule and an emergency had been imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on the pretext that the provincial government was siding with the terrorist narrative. Mr Fazl said that after the imposition of governor’s rule, nobody was talking about terrorism and everyone was discussing mineral resources. He said that for the imposition of the governor’s rule in a province, the governor had to write to the president but no such letter had been written. “The cabinet’s decision was turned into a summary and shared with the president, which is against legal and constitutional procedures,” he said. The JUI-F chief insisted that the president was required to state in writing that he agreed with the assertion that the civilian government had broken down, but no such written statement existed in that case. He also wondered why two systems had been introduced in the province, with one part placed under the governor’s rule and the other under an emergency. Mr Fazl claimed that Kohat division was also being included in the designated districts. He said that after he raised his voice, he had become a target of character assassination campaigns, with mainstream and social media being used against him. The JUI-F chief, however, said he had been facing such campaigns since the 1990s and would not be intimidated by such tactics. “Today, silence rules the political arena as everyone is silent but only we [JUI-F] are raising our voices,” he said. Mr Fazl said another narrative was being promoted, accusing the JUI-F of having a soft corner for militants. “You should be ashamed of saying this as the JUI-F is playing a pivotal role in opposing armed struggle among people,” he said. He said such archaic tactics would not intimidate them. “If you want a fight, just dare to lay a hand on us and then you will witness the lengths to which our workers will go,” he said. Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

items.title: Balochistan begins polio drive amid Afghan spillover fears
items.description: QUETTA: Balochistan on Monday launched its fifth seven-day anti-polio campaign of the year, targeting more than 2.2 million children across 31 districts amid concerns over the possible spread of the virus from neighbouring Afghanistan. Balochistan Health Secretary Mujeebur Rehman announced the launch, warning that more than 50 polio cases reported in Afghanistan this year had increased the risk of cross-border transmission, particularly in Chaman and Qila Abdullah. Speaking to the media at the campaign’s inauguration in Quetta, he said more than 8,880 vaccination teams had been deployed to administer polio drops to children under five. Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) Balochistan Coordinator Inamul Haq and Quetta District Health Officer Dr Aimal Mandokhail were also present. Mr Rehman said special attention was being given to districts bordering Afghanistan and sensitive areas adjoining Punjab. He stressed that frequent movement of people between the two countries could facilitate the spread of the virus, making stronger surveillance and targeted vaccination essential. More than 8,880 teams deployed across 31 districts He said Balochistan had reported no polio cases in the past 24 months, while environmental samples collected last month had also tested negative. He credited the progress to the sustained efforts of health authorities and vaccination teams but cautioned against complacency. The health secretary warned that children suffering from malnutrition and other health problems could be particularly vulnerable if the virus re-entered the province. He directed vaccination teams to perform their duties diligently and ensure that no eligible child was missed. He also stressed the need to strengthen routine immunisation alongside special campaigns to ensure lasting protection. Mr Rehman urged parents, teachers, religious scholars and community leaders to support the campaign and encourage families to get all children under five vaccinated. He said eradicating polio required collective efforts by the government, health authorities, international partners and the public. He reaffirmed that all available resources would be mobilised to keep Balochistan polio-free. Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

items.title: Partenariat Russie-Afrique : Moscou doit désormais passer à l’action sur le terrain économique pour matérialiser son intérêt pour le continent
items.description: De l’internationalisme soviétique aux ambitions géopolitiques de la Fédération de Russie, Moscou entretient avec l’Afrique une relation historiquement chargée de promesses, de solidarités politiques et de calculs stratégiques. Mais derrière les discours sur la fraternité des peuples, le bilan économique reste largement en deçà des attentes. Après trois sommets, l’heure est venue de confronter les déclarations aux réalisations et de demander des comptes sur les dividendes réels de cette longue proximité. ‎Il y a des amitiés diplomatiques qui se nourrissent de déclarations et d’autres qui se consolident à coups d’investissements, d’infrastructures, de transferts de technologies et d’emplois. Dans la compétition internationale pour les marchés, les ressources et les alliances, l’Afrique ne peut plus se satisfaire de poignées de main présidentielles, de communiqués exaltant une fraternité historique et de promesses dont les contours financiers restent parfois imprécis. La diplomatie économique ne se juge pas à la chaleur des accolades, mais à la matérialité des réalisations. ‎ ‎À cet égard, les annonces financières faites lors de plusieurs grands rendez-vous internationaux donnent une indication de l’ambition économique affichée par les partenaires du continent. Au sommet Chine-Afrique de Pékin, en septembre 2024, Xi Jinping a annoncé un soutien financier de 360 milliards de yuans sur trois ans, soit environ 50 milliards de dollars, comprenant des lignes de crédit, des aides et des investissements d’entreprises chinoises. Au sommet États-Unis-Afrique de décembre 2022, Washington a annoncé son intention de mobiliser 55 milliards de dollars sur trois ans. Au troisième Forum de coopération Inde-Afrique de 2015, New Delhi a proposé 10 milliards de dollars de lignes de crédit concessionnelles et 600 millions de dollars d’aide. Quant au sommet Africa Forward, organisé à Nairobi en mai 2026 par la France et le Kenya, il a enregistré des annonces de 23 milliards d’euros d’investissements, dont 14 milliards d’investissements français et 9 milliards d’investissements africains sur le continent. ‎ ‎Ces montants ne sont ni de même nature ni nécessairement intégralement décaissés. Certains relèvent de lignes de crédit, d’autres d’engagements publics, d’investissements privés ou d’aides au développement. Il serait donc hasardeux de les additionner ou de les présenter comme des réalisations acquises. Ils traduisent néanmoins une volonté de donner une dimension financière identifiable aux partenariats. C’est précisément sur ce terrain que la relation russo-africaine mérite un examen sans complaisance. Au terme de trois sommets, tenus à Sotchi en 2019, à Saint-Pétersbourg en 2023 et à Moscou en octobre 2026, le contraste demeure saisissant entre l’ambition géopolitique russe et la faiblesse des retombées économiques tangibles à l’échelle continentale. ‎ ‎Il ne s’agit pas d’affirmer que Moscou a officiellement promis zéro dollar d’investissement à l’Afrique. Les trois rencontres ont produit des accords, des annonces et des programmes de coopération. Mais force est de constater qu’elles n’ont pas débouché sur une enveloppe continentale d’investissements clairement chiffrée et comparable, dans sa lisibilité, aux annonces de plusieurs autres partenaires. Le problème n’est donc pas seulement celui des montants annoncés, mais surtout celui de leur traduction en projets financés, exécutés et bénéfiques aux populations. Une fraternité soviétique aux dividendes discutables ‎Pour comprendre ce décalage, il faut remonter aux premières heures des indépendances africaines. L’Union des républiques socialistes soviétiques (URSS) s’est alors positionnée comme un allié des peuples en lutte contre le colonialisme et l’impérialisme occidental. Dans le contexte de la guerre froide, Moscou a soutenu des mouvements de libération, accompagné certains régimes nouvellement indépendants et contribué à la formation de milliers de cadres africains. L’Université Patrice-Lumumba de Moscou est devenue l’un des symboles de cette coopération éducative et idéologique. ‎ ‎Cette solidarité n’était cependant pas désintéressée. Derrière l’internationalisme socialiste se jouait une bataille d’influence avec les puissances occidentales. L’Afrique constituait un espace stratégique de conquête diplomatique, militaire et idéologique. Les soutiens apportés aux mouvements révolutionnaires et aux régimes proches de Moscou participaient également à l’élargissement de la sphère d’influence soviétique. ‎ ‎Il serait toutefois historiquement injuste de soutenir que l’URSS n’a apporté aucune contribution matérielle au continent. Son assistance technique et financière a notamment participé à la réalisation du barrage d’Assouan en Égypte, tandis que son concours dans les domaines de l’enseignement supérieur, de la formation scientifique et de l’industrie a laissé des traces dans plusieurs pays africains. Mais ces réalisations, aussi importantes soient-elles, n’ont pas donné naissance à une dynamique économique continentale à la mesure des besoins structurels des États africains. La coopération a souvent privilégié les alliances politiques, militaires et idéologiques, sans produire une transformation suffisamment large et durable des économies africaines. ‎ ‎La disparition de l’URSS en 1991 aurait pu ouvrir une nouvelle page. Elle a plutôt interrompu une partie de ces relations, avant que la Fédération de Russie ne cherche progressivement à reconquérir le terrain diplomatique perdu. ‎Moscou revient, mais avec quels dividendes économiques ? ‎Depuis le sommet inaugural de Sotchi en 2019, Vladimir Poutine s’emploie à réinstaller la Russie dans le jeu africain. À cette occasion, il avait annoncé son ambition de doubler les échanges commerciaux russo-africains pour les porter à 40 milliards de dollars en cinq ans. En 2023, à Saint-Pétersbourg, Moscou a notamment mis en avant l’effacement de 23 milliards de dollars de dettes africaines et promis des livraisons gratuites de céréales à six pays. Pourtant, le bilan économique est resté en retrait des ambitions affichées. ‎ ‎Le troisième sommet, tenu à Moscou les 28 et 29 octobre 2026, était donc particulièrement attendu. Présenté comme une occasion de passer des déclarations aux réalisations, il a débouché sur une déclaration finale, un plan d’action 2027-2029 et plusieurs engagements sectoriels concernant notamment l’énergie, l’agriculture, la santé, l’industrie et les nouvelles technologies. Mais, une fois encore, la question essentielle demeure : quels financements sont effectivement mobilisés et quels projets seront concrètement exécutés ? ‎ ‎Certes, Moscou met en avant une progression de ses échanges avec le continent, estimés à environ 27 milliards de dollars en 2025. Mais ce chiffre doit être relativisé. Il reste inférieur à la barre des 40 milliards annoncée en 2019. Surtout, il s’agit d’un volume commercial et non d’un montant d’investissements russes en Afrique. Acheter du blé, vendre des engrais, des hydrocarbures ou des équipements militaires ne revient pas à financer des infrastructures, créer des unités industrielles ou transférer des capacités productives. ‎ ‎La structure des échanges mérite également attention. En 2024, les exportations russes vers l’Afrique ont atteint environ 24,3 milliards de dollars, contre 3,5 milliards d’importations en provenance du continent. Ce déséquilibre illustre une relation commerciale dans laquelle l’Afrique demeure davantage un débouché pour les produits russes qu’un partenaire bénéficiant d’une intégration économique équilibrée. ‎ ‎Plus préoccupant encore, la présence russe se manifeste avec davantage de visibilité dans les domaines militaire, sécuritaire, minier et énergétique que dans les secteurs directement associés à la transformation des conditions de vie des populations. Accords de défense, fournitures d’armements, coopération nucléaire, intérêts miniers et partenariats sécuritaires constituent les principaux leviers de cette reconquête. Moscou entend ainsi consolider son influence diplomatique et son accès aux ressources stratégiques africaines, dans un contexte de rivalité avec les puissances occidentales. ‎ ‎Là réside toute l’ambiguïté du partenariat. Moscou semble avoir davantage compris l’importance stratégique du sous-sol africain que l’urgence de contribuer à la transformation structurelle des économies qui en disposent. L’uranium, l’or, le pétrole, le gaz et les autres minerais stratégiques aiguisent les appétits. Mais à quel moment cette présence se traduit-elle par des routes, des chemins de fer, des hôpitaux, des universités, des centrales électriques, des industries de transformation et des emplois décents pour les jeunes Africains ? ‎ ‎Il ne s'agit pas de prétendre que la Russie n'a jamais participé à la réalisation d'infrastructures en Afrique. Le projet nucléaire d'El-Dabaa en Égypte, porté par Rosatom, en est une illustration contemporaine, même si l'installation est encore en construction. Mais un projet emblématique, aussi stratégique soit-il, ne saurait masquer l'insuffisance des investissements russes à l'échelle du continent. ‎ ‎L'opinion selon laquelle la Russie n'aurait construit ni routes ni hôpitaux en Afrique relève donc davantage d'une formule polémique que d'une vérité historique absolue. Elle traduit néanmoins une frustration réelle : celle de populations qui ne perçoivent pas, dans leur quotidien, des bénéfices proportionnels à l'intensité des discours sur l'amitié russo-africaine. ‎ ‎Cette situation interpelle également les dirigeants africains. ‎ ‎L'Afrique n'a pas à choisir entre Moscou, Pékin, Washington, New Delhi, Paris ou Ankara. Elle doit pouvoir commercer avec tous, négocier avec chacun et tirer profit de toutes les opportunités. Chaque partenariat doit être évalué à l'aune de ses retombées sur l’emploi, les infrastructures, le transfert de compétences, la transformation locale des matières premières et l'amélioration des conditions de vie. ‎ ‎La Russie a certes le droit de défendre ses intérêts géopolitiques et économiques. Mais l'Afrique a tout autant le droit d'exiger des contreparties à la hauteur de ses ressources et de son importance stratégique. La solidarité historique ne constitue pas un chèque en blanc. Pas plus que les souvenirs de la guerre froide ne peuvent tenir lieu de politique de développement au XXIe siècle. ‎ ‎Au fond, les trois sommets Russie-Afrique auront surtout démontré que les affinités politiques ne suffisent pas à bâtir une prospérité partagée. La fraternité proclamée dans les palais présidentiels doit désormais descendre dans les quartiers populaires, les campagnes, les usines, les hôpitaux et les écoles. Elle doit se mesurer en investissements productifs, en infrastructures fonctionnelles, en emplois créés et en vies transformées. ‎ ‎L'Afrique n'a plus besoin de partenaires qui lui rappellent indéfiniment leur amitié. Elle a besoin de partenaires qui acceptent d'investir dans son avenir. À force de célébrer une coopération dont les dividendes économiques restent si peu perceptibles, le discours russo-africain risque de finir par sentir le roussi. ‎ Donatien FOFANA, ‎Pour Netafrique.net L’article Partenariat Russie-Afrique : Moscou doit désormais passer à l'action sur le terrain économique pour matérialiser son intérêt pour le continent est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Montée des couleurs à l’hôtel administratif du Kadiogo : « le Burkina Faso est un pays fréquenté et fréquentable », Pingdwendé Gilbert OUEDRAOGO
items.description: Le Ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Porte-parole du Gouvernement, Pingdwendé Gilbert OUEDRAOGO a pris part ce lundi 02 novembre 2026 à la traditionnelle montée mensuelle des couleurs aux côtés de ses collègues ministres chargées de la Transition digitale (Dr Aminata ZERBO/SABANÉ), de la Famille (Lieutenant-Colonel Passowendé Pélagie KABRÉ/KABORÉ) et du personnel des départements ministériels logés à l’hôtel administratif du Kadiogo. A l’issue du cérémonial de montée des couleurs, le Ministre Porte-parole a adressé un message aux serviteurs du peuple. Il a d’abord rendu un vibrant hommage aux Forces de défense et de sécurité qui ont célébré le 1er novembre leur 66e anniversaire. Bien que des défis sécuritaires demeurent, de belles avancées ont été faites sur le terrain de la reconquête du territoire et de la lutte contre le terrorisme, ce qui a permis le retour progressif de nombreux déplacés chez eux et la reprise des activités dans les localités reconquises. ​ En second lieu, le chef du Département chargé du tourisme a martelé que le Burkina Faso force l’admiration sur la scène internationale et reste un pays fréquenté et fréquentable. Pour preuve, la tenue concomitante de trois grands événementiels à cette période vient battre en brèche le narratif tendant à « peindre en rouge » le Pays des hommes intègres. Il s’agit de la tenue de la 18e édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO) qui se déroule du 30 octobre au 8 novembre avec une quinzaine de pays participants ; le 37e Tour international du Faso qui se tient à la même période et qui connait la participation de 80 cyclistes venant d’une dizaine de pays d’Afrique, d’Europe et marqué par le retour de l’Union cycliste internationale (UCI) ; et enfin l’organisation de la 15e édition du Symposium international de sculpture sur granite de Laongo qui réunit 45 sculpteurs de 13 pays d’Afrique, d’Asie, d’Europe et d’Amérique du 02 au 23 novembre. L’ensemble de ces événements qui accueillent des participants venus des quatre coins du monde, prouvent que le pays garde toute sa place sur la scène internationale. ​Pour terminer, le Porte-parole du Gouvernement a invité l’ensemble du personnel à aborder la fin de l’année avec rigueur, solidarité et amour du prochain. >, foi du Ministre Pingdwendé.
